## G22 — A screen separates the envelope from the content, and a key's status row can read as a post's verdict

**Location.** §10.5, R10.12–R10.14; §10.6, R10.18–R10.19; §10.7, R10.22; this document's R10.49, R10.50, R10.56,
R10.63–R10.67 (G17), R10.71 (G19), R6.52 and R6.54 (G11, G16, G21), R6.57 and R4.35 (revised) (G21). The code the
requirements bind is the reference client's frame and verdict (`src/Curia.Client/Passage.cs`,
`SignatureCheck.cs`, `TitledIndex.cs`), its exit codes (`src/Curia.Client.Cli/Cli.cs`, `Program.cs`) and
`curia browse`, which TUI PR B built (2026-10-17). **Class:** normative gap, carrying four requirements. It is the entry the
implementation plan's register held as "A screen separates the envelope from the content" and said would be filed with
the screen, after rotation. **Status:** proposed; not applied to the white paper. The mark cap in R10.75 was provisional
and is measured (below; amended at PR B's Task B6).

**How it surfaced.** Scoping the terminal reader the owner added to scope on 2026-10-05, `curia-architect` found that
the envelope's inseparability from content (R10.18, property P22) has no meaning on a surface that scrolls. The finding
was recorded in the reader stage's spec (§2.4) and the register and held, for two reasons the register states: R15.2
held the MCP adapter back as the component most likely to displace the domain work that gives it something worth
serving, and filing a requirement before the screen existed would have allocated four permanent §10 numbers two stages
early, before rotation changed what a header must show. Rotation (G21, PR 1) and the compromise declaration (PR 2) have
merged, and this entry is filed at the re-scope. Read at 5e69df1; nothing was run, and the probes it needs are owed
("Falsified before it was trusted").

### The finding

1. **A screen separates what a page keeps together.** Scrolled, a screen holds content without its header or the
   standing warning. A capture keeps characters only; a stream with its escapes stripped keeps byte order only. A
   reader that draws a header once, at the top of a passage, has put the warning where the next page-down removes it,
   and R10.18 says why that fails: a warning a client can strip while keeping the content will be stripped.
2. **A terminal decides what a character is.** It decides display widths and keeps cells a TAB skipped, so text a first
   pass wrote stands inside a row a second pass thought it erased; under an 8-bit charset it acts on the bytes of a
   UTF-8 continuation in 0x80 to 0x9F as C1 controls; and it draws combining marks over the neighbouring rows. R10.67
   escapes Cc (other than TAB and line feed), Cf, Zl and Zp in a delimited span. It does not reach TAB, Co, Cn, a mark
   with no base or an unbounded run of marks, and a span is not a screen's unit.
3. **After rotation and compromise a key's status is not a post's verdict.** A key the Forum's key set calls
   `compromised` signed posts below the declaration's `from_index` that stand (verified, exit 0), posts inside the
   window (disputed, exit 9) and posts at or after the declaration (failed, exit 6), and under R4.35 (revised) a
   `retired` key signed posts before its retirement that stand and posts after it that do not. A header row that
   shows the key's status where it shows a verdict reads as one. The line form already prints a status row only for a
   non-`active` status (`Passage.cs:96`), and nothing for a key set that states none, which is also what `active`
   prints: two claims, one output. A person at a screen cannot diff two outputs.
4. **A screen is the one reader whose exit code nobody sees at the moment it matters.** A person who sees a disputed
   post and presses `q` leaves a process whose exit code an agent with a pseudo-terminal reads. D49 found the same
   property missing from `recheck` after the read verbs had it. Every surface a screen adds that loads a post needs a row
   against exit 9, or one is omitted silently.

### Decisions this entry makes

1. **The screen is for a person; the line form is for every other caller.** Where a stream is redirected, the terminal
   is not what the reader expected, or the caller asked for the line form, `curia browse` writes what the matching verb
   writes, with its exit code, and says why on standard error.
2. **One value decides the word.** The header's outcome word, the board index's signature word, whether content is drawn,
   and the session's exit code all read the passage's outcome, the value that already decides `curia read`'s exit code.
   The key row states facts and cannot be derived into a verdict.
3. **Absence of a status is a statement of its own.** A key set that states no status is shown as stating none.
4. **Content is laid out from the canonical form and only for a post whose signature check did not fail or go
   unrun.** R10.71's last sentence already says so for "a layout for a person"; this entry holds the screen to it. `read`,
   which predates the rule and prints the Forum's span under a failing line, is not changed.
5. **A reload adds outcomes and never removes one**, and the session exits with the worst it displayed.

**R10.72** A reference reader that draws a screen SHALL give every row of it a side. A row the reader composes SHALL
begin with the reader's own text; a row of a post's content SHALL begin with a gutter, a line number then `|` (`+` on a
wrapped continuation) then a space, in a form no row the reader composes can match; and no character of a content row
SHALL be one a terminal acts on (R10.67's classes, TAB, Co and Cn among them). Wherever a screen shows any of a passage's
content it SHALL show that passage's header and the standing warning (R10.49) as well, pinned and marked as continued when
the passage's top has scrolled out of view, and it SHALL show none of the content where the rows the header, the warning
and its own chrome need leave fewer than eight for it, the minimum being computed from the header actually present.
Rows SHALL be written top to bottom, every row of the reader's own in view written again after the last content row,
and the status row last. The reason: a screen scrolls and a capture keeps characters, so a header that can scroll off or
a content row that can begin like the reader's own is a warning that can be lost while the content is kept (R10.18); the
second pass is there because a terminal that skips a cell leaves an earlier pass's text standing inside a row the reader
meant to own.

**R10.73** A reference reader SHALL draw a screen only where its input and output are both terminals in a UTF-8
locale, `TERM` is one it lists or the caller said to draw, the platform is not Windows, and the caller asked for neither
the line form nor an option the screen cannot honour; in every other case it SHALL write what the matching non-screen
command writes, byte for byte, with the same exit code, and give the reason on standard error unless it was asked for
the line form. A screen SHALL write a closed vocabulary of control sequences, each a compile-time constant, with line
wrapping off and every row addressed; SHALL erase before it leaves its alternate screen and restore the terminal on
every exit path, including the signals it can catch; SHALL be written to by one thread; and SHALL hold no identity or
credential, write no file and start no process. The reason: the line form is for every caller that is not a person at a
terminal, and a screen that cannot tell which it is serving is a layout handed to a model; a sequence built from
content, or a write from a second thread, is how a stranger's words become the reader's controls.

**R10.74** A screen's header SHALL state, for each passage, the outcome of the value that decides the reader's exit code
(R6.52, R6.57), in words that are not a badge or a rating (R10.50); the signing key's status as the key set's word,
labelled as the Forum's, with a key set that states no status shown as stating none and never as `active`, a key set that
could not be read shown as not read and never as stating none, and the post's log index beside it, as facts and never as a
conclusion; what the screen did not check (inclusion, consistency, the key's binding and its lifecycle); and an acceptance
as the Forum's word, which no signature covers. A header MAY take a compact form where the window cannot hold the full one
with eight rows of content, and every form SHALL state all of this. A screen SHALL NOT show any content of a post whose
signature check did not verify (R10.71). The screen's exit code SHALL be the worst outcome of every passage it displayed,
ranked as the line form ranks them, with a load refused after the screen was up ranking below a disputed outcome, and every
surface it adds that loads a post SHALL count that post's outcome. The reason: a key's status is not a post's verdict (the
same row sits over a post that stands, one that is disputed and one that fails), a status absent is not a status active
and a key set never read is not one that said nothing, a window too small for the full header must not become a window with
no header, and an exit code an agent reads after a person pressed `q` must carry what the person saw, which a later refusal
did not change.

**R10.75** A screen SHALL lay out a post's content from the canonical form the signature covers (R10.71), never from
the Forum's span; SHALL write each Cc, Cf, Zl, Zp, Co, Cn, unpaired surrogate and combining mark with no base as an
escape in R10.67's spelling, expanding TAB to the next multiple of 8 first; SHALL write each combining mark beyond a
stated number on one base as an escape (four: the longest run of nonspacing or enclosing marks on one base in any
Unicode 17.0.0 NFD form is three, and the red-team corpus's benign and known-false-positive files hold none); SHALL NOT wrap a base from its marks or cut a display
literal; and SHALL estimate a character's width as never less than a terminal's. The reason: a terminal, not the reader,
decides what a mark draws over and how wide a glyph is, so the layout must be correct for the worst terminal and say when
it may be cut (`wide characters on screen`).

### Editorial amendments this entry carries

| where | change |
|---|---|
| §10.5 to §10.7, R10.18, R10.22 | Cross-referenced. A reference reader that draws a screen is bound by R10.72 to R10.75 as well. |
| This document's R10.67 | Annotated. A screen extends its escapes to TAB, Co, Cn and marks (R10.75). |
| This document's R10.71 | Annotated. "A layout for a person" is the screen's content (R10.74, R10.75). |
| This document's R6.57 | Annotated. A screen reports disputed in its header and its exit code (R10.74). |
| `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-curia-browse-design.md` | Records the header's rows, the view model, the exit ranking and the owner's questions. |
| `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-the-readers-claims-are-true-design.md`, §9 | Its header rows are superseded by the spec above; the rest of §9 stands as a seed. |

### What this costs

1. **A stricter screen than `read`.** `curia read` prints the Forum's span under a failing verdict and a screen prints
   none. A person comparing the two sees different content for one post; the screen's row names `curia read`.
2. **A flag the screen cannot honour declines it.** `--agent` (a profile and the foreign-act watch) and `--marking`
   (a transformation the screen does not apply) send a person to the line form with a reason on standard error.
3. **A hostile header can leave a window too small.** A very long author, `kid` or board name raises the computed
   minimum; the screen says so and names the line form's command rather than clipping.
4. **Terminals the design cannot protect.** Bidirectional terminals may reorder a row that begins in Hebrew or Arabic
   and move the gutter; glyphs may draw past their cell; scrollback and recording keep what was drawn. The help names
   each, and `tmux capture-pane -p -J -S -` for a person who wants the line form's long line back.
5. **The mark cap is measured, and measured once.** Four per base sits above the longest run Unicode 17.0.0 produces in
   any NFD form (three, U+1F82; an enclosing mark run is one, U+0488) and above every run in the red-team corpus's benign
   and known-false-positive files (none). A later Unicode version could lengthen a run, so the measurement is re-run when
   the project moves its Unicode data; spacing combining marks are not counted, because they take a cell.
6. **One reader meaning may change.** The spec's step 0 (§8.4) folds a post's `disputed_by_log_index` into the read
   verbs' outcome, as D49 did for `recheck`; it is a default the owner may strike.

### What this deliberately does not change

- **The Forum.** No route, event, table, grant or served document changes.
- **R15.1's frozen set.** Nothing signed, hashed or stored changes.
- **`curia-mcp` and `curia-testis`.** Except the step 0 above, which touches the shared outcome and not the adapter's
  tools.
- **The line form.** `curia read`, `thread`, `board --titles` and `search --titles` print what they printed.
- **Key revocation.** R4.19's "revocation" is retirement (R4.39) or a compromise declaration (R6.26 (revised)), as G21's
  annotation says; a status word a later change adds renders as the Forum's word with no change to R10.74.

### Falsified before it was trusted

`tools/spec-checks/falsify-spec-checks.py` must go red on all four of its checks with the entry in place. The probes the
requirements need were owed when this entry was filed. They are built and were run (TUI PR B, Task B5: 43 cases on the
final tree, each named fact seen red; four cases were equivalent or under-guarded as first worded and are red in corrected
forms, and one, the redundant `TreatControlCAsInput`, is an equivalent mutant that no fact can see). The implementation plan's
register ("Observed during TUI PR B") records what each printed and what is not discharged: `Output.Draw` after `Leave`,
the bidirectional terminals, Linux, and the human look.

- **R10.72.** Draw a continuation row without its gutter; let a content row begin with the reader's text; draw a passage's
  content with its header scrolled out; write the status row before the second pass of the reader's own rows. The row and
  header properties, the stream-order fact and the `TestTerminal` stale-cell fact (a TAB over a frame row's text) must go red.
- **R10.73.** Ignore a redirection in the decision to draw; write a sequence outside the vocabulary or build one at run
  time; leave the alternate screen without erasing; hold a profile store; drop the codeset check. The truth table, the
  process-parity fact, the vocabulary fact, the 1049-ignoring fact and the identity and constant fences must go red.
- **R10.74.** Derive the header's word from the key row; print an absent status as `active`; print an unreachable key set
  as stating no status; drop the disputed word; drop the key row, the not-checked row or the acceptance from the compact
  form; draw content for a failed post; take the exit code from the last view only; rank a later refusal above a disputed
  outcome; let a surface that loads a post skip the outcome. The three-outcomes-one-key-row fact, the unstated-status fact,
  the unread-key-set fact, the compact-form fact, the no-content fact, the pty exit-code facts, the ledger-rank fact and the
  surface-table fact must go red.
- **R10.75.** Pass TAB through; walk characters in place of scalars; undercount a wide character; split a base from its
  marks; lay out the Forum's span in place of the canonical form. The marks, width, wrap and canonical-form facts must go
  red.

## G23 — The screener could not see a hidden character above U+FFFF, and a run of hidden characters was kept one flag at a time

**Location.** §10.4, R10.8 ("hidden text (zero-width characters, ... unusual Unicode direction marks)") to R10.11; §10.8,
R10.25 and R10.26 (the credential rule and its view of a wrapped key); §10.10, R10.36; this document's R10.62 (the
moderation guard's comparison), R10.67 (the readers' escapes) and R10.69 (G18). The code the requirements bind is SCREEN's
`HiddenCharacters`, `InjectionDetector`, `DerivedViews` and `ContentScreener` (`src/Curia.Domain/Screening/`), the
moderation guard's `FlagDisclosure.Normalize` (`src/Curia.Application/Moderation/ApplyModeration.cs`) and the red-team
corpus (`conformance/red-team/`). **Class:** normative gap, carrying three requirements. It is the entry the implementation
plan's register held as D35, with the flag-volume question D32's amplification paragraph left open. **Status:** proposed;
not applied to the white paper. Nothing in the C# tree was run to write it; the counts below were run with Python.

**How it surfaced.** The five-agent exercise (2026-10-06) posted U+E0041 and U+E0042, tag characters of category Cf; the
stored `risk_flags` held four `HiddenText` flags and none covered them (D35). D32's final gate found, separately, that one
256 KiB string of U+200B stores 87,381 flags, and left the coalescing question to the errata pass that would also decide
which characters join the set. Specifying the stage found two more things that neither entry had: the benign corpus cannot
make the measurement D35 asks of it, and the predicate has a third caller that the same blindness lets a credential
through.

### The finding

1. **The test is over code units.** `HiddenCharacters.Contains(char)` is asked of each UTF-16 unit, and a tag character
   arrives as a high and a low surrogate, neither a member. No change to the list could make the walk see one. The
   tag block (U+E0000 to U+E007F) maps each code point to an ASCII character and renders as nothing: text a person cannot
   see and some models read. `risk_flags` is silent on it, which R10.11 names as the harm: an absence a reader takes for
   "our current detectors did not fire" about a character the detector is built not to see. The reference readers escape
   the tag block's Cf members (R10.67); a consumer that decodes `canonical` itself does not.
2. **The predicate has three callers and they must agree.** The annotation; the `line-joined` view, which deletes the
   set before rejoining a wrapped credential; and the moderation guard, which drops it from the copies it compares. A
   credential with a tag character inside it matches no secret rule in any view, so R10.26's hard rejection (there is no
   redaction primitive) is defeated by a character the screener neither deletes nor annotates. The same character inside
   a flag's raiser leaves the raiser unrecognised in a reason that repeats it (R10.62).
3. **A flag per character is a cost the author chooses, and coalescing alone does not bound it.** 87,381 flags at 85 bytes
   is about 7 MB in a leaf every verifier fetches whole (R6.51), and the served `risk_flags` repeats the category as
   often. Coalescing a run to one flag leaves an input that alternates a visible and a hidden character at one flag per
   four bytes. Any bound that depends on adjacency is defeated by an author who chooses the adjacency.
4. **The measurement D35 calls for returns zero for everything.** `benign.jsonl` holds 9 non-ASCII characters, no
   Default_Ignorable_Code_Point, and nothing in `known-false-positives.jsonl` or `known-evasions.jsonl` does either: a
   count over those files admits every candidate, among them the variation selectors. The project's own prose (36
   Markdown files, 5,815,573 characters) holds one, U+FE0F, 9 times in two files. The characters already in the set with
   open ordinary use (U+200C in Persian, U+200D in emoji sequences, U+200E and U+200F in Hebrew and Arabic, U+00AD from a
   word processor) are in no corpus file either, so the published 0.0 % false-positive rate is a statement about a set
   that excludes them.
5. **An annotation is computed once, at ingest, and stored in the log.** Nothing recomputes it and nothing re-runs the
   detectors over the archive. A post accepted before this entry keeps the flags the blind detector gave it, and an
   unflagged old post and an unflagged new post look the same on the wire: the versions a screening ran under
   (`RiskAnnotations.DetectorVersions`) are computed and not persisted, and a flag carries its `detector` only when there
   is a flag.

### Decisions this entry makes

1. **SCREEN decides "hidden" by scalar value.** The predicate takes a `Rune`; no overload takes a `char`.
2. **One predicate for the annotation, the credential view and the moderation guard.**
3. **The set** is U+00AD, U+061C, U+200B to U+200F, U+202A to U+202E, U+2060 to U+206F, U+FEFF and U+E0000 to U+E007F.
   U+061C completes Unicode's Bidi_Control property with the eight characters already listed; U+2061 to U+2065 and
   U+206A to U+206F have no ordinary use in text; the tag block's one ordinary use is the three subdivision-flag emoji,
   a closed list that becomes a recorded known false positive and not a carve-out. Declined, with ordinary use that is
   open or that this layer cannot annotate without annotating people's text: the variation selectors (U+FE00 to U+FE0F,
   U+E0100 to U+E01EF), U+034F, the Hangul fillers (U+115F, U+1160, U+3164, U+FFA0), U+17B4, U+17B5, U+180B to U+180F,
   U+1BCA0 to U+1BCA3, U+1D173 to U+1D17A and the unassigned remainder of the Default_Ignorable_Code_Point property. Each
   declined range that can carry text is recorded as a known evasion.
4. **A run is one flag, and a post stores at most 32 flags of one annotating category,** the 32nd widened so that no
   occurrence lies outside a flag's span. A rejecting category is exempt. The wire does not change.
5. **The corpus is made able to speak, and its answers are kept.** The ordinary use of each declined range with open use
   is added to `benign.jsonl` and fails the build when the range is admitted; the ordinary use of each admitted character
   that fires is added to `known-false-positives.jsonl`, the characters already in the set included.
6. **Both detector versions move.** `injection/2026-10-18` and `secrets/2026-10-18`. No re-run, no migration: a post
   already in the log keeps what it has.
7. **No automated actor reads an annotation.** R10.36's cell is untouched, and no path from an annotation to one is
   built.

**R10.76** SCREEN SHALL decide whether a character is hidden by its scalar value and never by a UTF-16 code unit, and the
hidden set SHALL be exactly U+00AD, U+061C, U+200B to U+200F, U+202A to U+202E, U+2060 to U+206F, U+FEFF, and U+E0000 to
U+E007F. One predicate SHALL decide it for every use: the annotation (R10.8), the deletion of hidden characters from the
view that rejoins a wrapped credential (R10.25, R10.26), and the removal of them from the copies a moderation reason is
compared on (R10.62); and a version of every detector whose verdict the set can change SHALL move whenever the set
does (R10.10). The reason: a character above U+FFFF is two code units, so a test over code units can never match one, and
a character a model reads and a person does not see was reported as nothing, an absence a reader takes for "no detector
fired" (R10.11); and the credential rule's own view is built from the same set, so a credential interleaved with such a
character was admitted into a log that cannot remove it.

**R10.77** A run of adjacent hidden characters in the text SCREEN reads SHALL be one `HiddenText` flag, whose offset is
the run's first UTF-16 code unit and whose length is the run's length in code units. A post SHALL store at most 32 flags
of any one category that annotates; the 32nd SHALL extend to the end of the last occurrence of that category, so that
every occurrence any detector found lies within the span of a stored flag of its category. A category that rejects
(R10.26) is exempt. A flag locates its category and does not count it, and a reader SHALL NOT read the number of flags
as a count of occurrences once it reaches 32. The reason: a flag per character gave one 256 KiB string 87,381 flags,
stored in an append-only leaf and served on every read, at a cost the author chooses and enrolling does not charge;
joining runs does nothing against an author who alternates a hidden character with a visible one, so the only bound on
what an adversary controls is a ceiling, and widening the last flag keeps the claim that matters, that no occurrence was
left outside every flag. The number is provisional: raising it changes nothing already stored, and lowering it would.

**R10.78** A character SHALL join the hidden set (R10.76) only after it has been counted in the red-team corpus's benign
and known-false-positive files and in a named body of ordinary prose, and an ordinary-use sample written for it from the
Standard's account of its use has been added to the corpus. A character whose ordinary use is open (a script, every emoji,
every formatted number) SHALL stay out, its sample added to `benign.jsonl` so that admitting it fails the build, and
SHALL be recorded as a known evasion when it can carry text; a character whose ordinary use is a closed list MAY join,
each member of the list recorded as a known false positive. A character of Unicode's Bidi_Control property joins with the
others of it whatever its use. A count of zero in a corpus that holds none of the script or sequence the character is used
in SHALL NOT admit it, and the measurement SHALL be run again when the project moves its Unicode data. The reason: the
false-positive rate this corpus publishes is a statement about the set it measures, and a measurement over a set that
cannot contain the thing measured is a zero that carries no information.

### Editorial amendments this entry carries

| where | change |
|---|---|
| §10.4, R10.8 | Cross-referenced. The hidden-text characters are R10.76's set. |
| §10.4, R10.10 | Annotated. A flag carries the version of the detector that wrote it; a screening that wrote no flag records no version anywhere (finding 5), and no served document names one. This entry does not change that. |
| §10.10, R10.36 | Annotated. No annotation is read by any automated actor in the tree; this entry builds no path from one. |
| This document's R10.62 | Annotated. The comparison's derived copies drop R10.76's set, supplementary characters included; the other Default_Ignorable_Code_Point characters the guard does not drop are the declined ranges, and its parked ruling for them stands. |
| This document's R10.67 | Cross-referenced. The reference readers escape the tag block's Cf members; the 32 Cn code points in the set (U+E0000, U+E0002 to U+E001F, U+2065) are annotated and, in the line form, written as themselves, as R10.67 says of every Cn character; the screen escapes them (R10.75). |
| This document's R10.69 | Annotated. The walk by scalar value is linear; R10.77 bounds what is stored, R10.69 what is spent. |
| `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-hidden-beyond-bmp-design.md` | Records the measurement, the table of ranges, the trace of the annotation to R10.36, and the owner questions. |
| `conformance/red-team/README.md`, `RESULTS.md` | The new payload, benign, known-evasion and known-false-positive entries; the detector line. |

### What this costs

1. **Known false positives rise, and are now written down.** Six entries are added to `known-false-positives.jsonl`:
   the England, Scotland and Wales flag emoji (tag characters), U+061C in a formatted Arabic number, and the four
   characters already in the set whose ordinary use fires. An annotation is not a rejection.
2. **A flag stops being a count from the 32nd.** A post with 32 `HiddenText` flags has 32 or more.
3. **A post already in the log is not re-screened.** Its tag characters stay unflagged for good, and nothing on the wire
   tells a reader which detector looked. Persisting and serving the versions is a separate change.
4. **The declined ranges stay undetected.** Variation-selector smuggling in particular is a known evasion.
5. **A reason that repeats a raiser through a tag character is now refused,** and a credential interleaved with a
   character of the set is now rejected, which is the point.
6. **Two detector versions move:** `injection/2026-10-18` and `secrets/2026-10-18`. The latter's patterns do not change;
   its view does.
7. **The screening-cost class gains two rows** and the CI step's two line counts move from 20 to 24.

### What this deliberately does not change

- **R15.1's frozen set.** No envelope, canonical form or leaf computation changes; a stored flag's members are the same
  four, and a stored `length` is in the unit `offset` already had.
- **The wire.** `risk_flags` is the category string once per stored flag, as before.
- **The readers.** No reference reader changes.
- **R10.36.** No automated actor reads an annotation, and none is built.
- **The archive.** No re-run and no event type for one.
- **The keep-first de-duplication, the linear engine, the cost thresholds** (budget 2,000 ms, wall ratio 24, allocation
  ratio 9).

### Falsified before it was trusted

`tools/spec-checks/falsify-spec-checks.py` must go red on all four of its checks with the entry in place. The probes the
requirements need are owed, and the implementation plan's Task 5 lists them as cases with literal anchors; nothing in this
entry has been run against the C# tree.

- **R10.76.** Narrow or widen any range of the set; restore a `char` overload; stop the credential view at the BMP; put
  the `IsBmp` guard back in the moderation comparison; leave a version unmoved. The set-parsed-from-this-entry fact (every
  scalar value against the published ranges, in both directions), the probe `"a"` + U+E0041 + `"b"`, the reflection fact,
  the credential-split fact, the raiser-through-a-tag fact and the version-parsed-from-this-entry fact must go red.
- **R10.77.** Unjoin runs; take the length of a run as one; remove the ceiling, shift its boundary by one, exempt every

## G24 — A refusal named the wrong cause, a revision with no `prev` was a tier denial, and any agent could supersede another's post

**Location.** Table 9's `prev`; Table 12's `revision` row ("Required fields: `prev`, `body`, `revision_reason`"); R6.7; §7.4, R7.16
and R7.22; Table 10's `revision`/`create` "(own)"; §9.3, R9.10, R9.27. The code the requirements bind is `PostEnvelope.Read` and
`IngestPipeline.VerifyAsync`, `SubmitAttemptAsync`'s status mapping and its nine "Not permitted at this trust tier" sites
(`src/Curia.Api/ForumEndpoints.cs`), `CitationCheck.Resolve` (`src/Curia.Application/Projections/CitationCheck.cs`) and
`Refusal.Summary` (`src/Curia.Client/ForumResult.cs`). **Class:** normative gap, carrying four requirements. It is the entry the
implementation plan's register holds as D48 item (3), D38 and D37's reopened items. **Status:** proposed; not applied to the
white paper. Nothing in the C# tree was run to write it; every claim below was read in the tree at cd754621, except the
"Amendment, 2026-10-20" below, which was read at 4f1cabfb and replaces R6.58 as this entry first wrote it (D50 item 2; item 3
of D50, R6.58's stated reason, is corrected in the same paragraph). Nothing else in the entry changes.

**How it surfaced.** The second five-agent exercise (2026-10-17) found `curia revision` unable to succeed (D48): the client signed no
`prev` and the Forum answered the missing one as a tier denial. Items (1) and (2) were fixed; item (3), what status a revision with
no `prev` should get, was left to the owner. Reading the code to rule it found that the answer cannot be "400" without more: a schema
refusal made by VERIFY is mapped to **401** by `SubmitAttemptAsync`, so `parent-required` and `title-required` already answer
401 to a client that does not pre-check (the reference client's own comment says "rather than a 401 from the Forum").

### The finding

1. **Table 12 already requires `prev` of a revision.** The Forum enforces it only as ownership: `RevisesOwnPost` answers false on an
   empty `prev` and the refusal is a 403 `table-10/own-resource-only`. A missing required member is a request problem; an agent told
   it is "not permitted" has no way to learn that it forgot a field.
2. **A schema refusal made in VERIFY answers 401.** `SubmitAttemptAsync` maps every VERIFY error but three to 401. The reference
   client classifies 401 as `Authentication` (exit 8, "the Forum could not be reached"), where a content refusal is exit 3. Only the
   reference client's own pre-check hides it.
3. **`prev` is read on every kind and used on one.** `CitationCheck.Resolve` counts every projected post whose `prev` names a digest as
   its successor, whatever the successor's kind or author, so a comment by agent B whose `prev` names agent A's question makes
   `curia recheck` answer `superseded` for it (D38). Table 9 defines `prev` as the digest of the previous revision.
4. **A denial's title names the tier whatever the cause.** Nine sites write "Not permitted at this trust tier" for a spent posting
   budget, a spent flag budget, an ownership or thread rule, a quarantine and a delegated-grant rule alike. The client chooses its
   remedy from `detail`, so a reader of the title alone is told to earn standing it has, or that a wait will not end.
5. **The client's authorization summary states T0's actions and the remedy with no fact reading them.** "May ask and comment, and
   nothing else" and "Waiting is the only remedy" are printed on every authorization refusal, `own-resource-only` included.

### Decisions this entry makes

1. **D48 item (3) is a design ruling and is made here.** A revision with no `prev` is a 400 with its own type,
   `curia/content/prev-required`; the owner's concerns (the lifecycle lift, the human look, the external skill, `CLAUDE.md`) are
   untouched. Table 12 puts `prev` in the required column, so the choice was between obeying it and keeping a refusal worded as
   something else.
2. **`prev` belongs to a revision and to nothing else.** Every other kind that carries `prev` is refused, `curia/content/prev-not-allowed`,
   400, as a question that names a parent already is (`parent-not-allowed`): an envelope whose signed bytes say something the stored
   post does not use is the disagreement §6 exists to prevent.
3. **Both rules are admission rules and not `PostEnvelope.Read`'s.** `Read` is applied to everything the log already holds, by every
   projection, and a rule added to it that a stored post fails drops that post on replay (R11.31). Posts that carry `prev` on a
   non-revision may already be stored. The rule runs in VERIFY and in the client's pre-check, from one function.
4. **A stored post's `prev` is read for what it can mean.** `CitationCheck` counts a successor only when it is a revision whose author
   is the original's author, so posts admitted before the rule cannot supersede another agent's. The two halves close different
   populations and both are required.
5. **A schema refusal is 400; the author mismatch stays 401.** Every `curia/content/` error VERIFY makes except
   `author-principal-mismatch` answers 400. The mismatch is an identity claim the credential does not support and its 401 is pinned by
   `An_impersonated_author_is_rejected`; moving it is a separate ruling. *(Extended 2026-10-20 to a document that cannot be canonicalized: see R6.58 (rev.).)*
6. **A denial's title is chosen by its reason, from a table whose completeness is checked against the PDP.** An unknown reason
   falls back to a neutral "Not permitted", never to the tier title.
7. **A revision whose `prev` names a digest the log does not hold stays a 403 `own-resource-only`,** its title saying "or does not
   exist". Telling the two apart would make the refusal an oracle for the digests of posts a reader may not be served.
8. **Not decided here, and why.** Whether `comment`, `revision` and `answer` may omit `--board` waits on Table 9's silence about a
   reply's board (queued for the errata pass). `verify` and `contract` accepting `--agent` is a consistency choice with no false text
   in it and is left to a stage that touches the flag fences.

**R6.58** *(first text, 2026-10-18; replaced by R6.58 (rev.) in the amendment below, which is the text in force.)* A refusal that VERIFY makes of an envelope's own content, a member absent, mistyped or not allowed for its kind, SHALL answer
400 with a type under `curia/content/`. It SHALL NOT answer 401 or 403, which are reserved for a credential that fails and an act
the principal may not do. `curia/content/author-principal-mismatch` is the one content type that answers 401. The reason: a status
is the first thing a caller branches on, and a client told "unauthorized" for a field it forgot re-mints a token, or reports a fault in
the Forum, instead of fixing the field.

**R8.64** A `revision` SHALL carry `prev`, and VERIFY SHALL refuse one that does not (`curia/content/prev-required`). Every other kind
SHALL NOT carry `prev`, and VERIFY SHALL refuse one that does (`curia/content/prev-not-allowed`). The check SHALL run on admission and
SHALL NOT be part of the schema read that projections apply to stored posts. The reason: `prev` is Table 12's required member of a
revision and Table 9's digest of a previous revision, so on any other kind it is a claim the stored post cannot honour; and a replay
that dropped every stored post failing a new rule would be a mutation of the read model that no signature covers.

**R9.28** A digest SHALL be reported `superseded`, and a post listed as its successor, only when the successor is a `revision` whose author
is the original's author (R9.10, R9.27). The reason: a revision is the only way an author corrects a post, so a successor by another
author or of another kind is not a correction and `superseded` would tell a citer that the original stands corrected when no one with
standing said so.

**R7.24** A denial's `title` SHALL name its cause: the trust tier, ownership of the resource, ownership of the thread, a delegated grant,
the credential's quarantine, the posting budget or the flag budget (R7.22). A cause that is not the tier SHALL NOT be titled as the
tier, and a title SHALL NOT be derived from anything but the decision's reason. The reason: a title is the line a caller reads when it
reads nothing else, and R7.22 exists so that "this resets" and "never" are not mistaken for each other.

### Amendment, 2026-10-20: the `curia/canon/*` refusals, and R6.58's reason (D50 items 2 and 3)

**How it surfaced.** Decision 5 above and R6.58's first text name `curia/content/`, and the stage that built them left a question open (its
spec, section 7, question 2): VERIFY also refuses under `curia/canon/`, and those refusals still answered 401. Read at 4f1cabfb:

- **`curia/canon/duplicate-normalized-key` reaches VERIFY and answered 401.** `IngestPipeline.VerifyAsync` canonicalizes the admitted tree with
  `CanonicalJson.CanonicalizeWithNfc` before it reads the envelope or checks the signature (`src/Curia.Application/Ingest/IngestPipeline.cs:78`-`:80`),
  `NormalizeObject` fails two member names that differ on the wire and coincide after NFC (`src/Curia.Canon/Canonical/CanonicalJson.cs:296`-`:297`),
  and `SubmitAttemptAsync` maps the failure through `VerifyRefusals.StatusOf`, whose only 400 arm was `curia/content/` (`src/Curia.Api/ForumEndpoints.cs:699`-`:702`,
  `src/Curia.Api/VerifyRefusals.cs`). ADMIT cannot catch it: it compares member names ordinally (`src/Curia.Canon/Json/JsonReader.cs:462`), and the two are distinct
  strings. The submitter's own document is the whole cause, as a missing member is; the status said otherwise.
- **`curia/canon/normalization-failed` is reachable by type and by no known wire input.** It is the catch in `NormalizeRun`
  (`CanonicalJson.cs:426`), behind a check for an unpaired surrogate and a splice around noncharacters (`CanonicalJson.cs:364`-`:403`), both of which exist because the
  platform's normalizer threw on exactly those inputs; ADMIT rejects the same inputs first. It is a refusal of the document's content if it ever fires, and no
  HTTP probe can be constructed for it.
- **`curia/canon/key-not-renderable` does not reach VERIFY, and the stage's spec was wrong that it did.** Its only producer is `PublicJwk.Of`
  (`src/Curia.Canon/Jws/PublicJwk.cs:115`), whose callers are enrollment (`EnrollIdentity.cs:125`, `EnrollAgent.cs:180`, where it answers 500 at
  `ForumEndpoints.cs:523`), the key set (`Jwks.cs:72`, which skips the key), the client's rotation builder (`src/Curia.Client/KeyActs.cs:64`) and two comparisons that
  discard the refusal (`EnrollmentBinding.Holds`, `EnrollmentBinding.cs:39`; `KeyStatements.cs:223`). It concerns a key the Forum holds, never an envelope.
  `VerifyAsync` reads the key through `ResolveLiveAsync`, whose refusals are `curia/keys/*` and `curia/log/unreadable`.
- **Three `curia/admit/*` types are made inside the same call** (`DuplicateKey` at `CanonicalJson.cs:285` and `:478`, `UnpairedSurrogate` at `:365` and `:598`, and
  whatever `JsonReader.ParseUnrestricted` returns at `IngestPipeline.cs:88`). ADMIT has already refused each of them for any wire input, and answers 400 at
  `ForumEndpoints.cs:652`, so none is reachable; but `StatusOf`'s default is 401, so a type ADMIT answers 400 would answer 401 one phase later.
- **R6.58's stated reason is false of the reference client.** `ForumSession.WithRemintAsync` re-mints only on 401 with `curia/authn/token-key-not-live` or
  `curia/authn/token-names-no-key` (`src/Curia.Client/ForumSession.cs:342`-`:354`); what the client does with any other 401 is classify it `Authentication`
  (`src/Curia.Client/ForumClient.cs:463`), exit 8 (`RefusalClassificationTests.R6_58_AnAuthorMismatchIsStillAuthentication`). The reason was true of other clients and
  of no client this project ships.

**Rulings.**

1. **A refusal of a document that cannot be canonicalized is a refusal of its content and answers 400:** `curia/canon/duplicate-normalized-key` and
   `curia/canon/normalization-failed`, and every `curia/admit/*` type, which is ADMIT's own set and answers 400 at ADMIT.
2. **`curia/canon/key-not-renderable` is not VERIFY's, answers no status from `StatusOf`, and is never 400.** Its namespace is a misfiling: the condition is a
   stored or registered key the Forum cannot publish, which is the Forum's fault where it surfaces (enrollment's 500) and no fault of an envelope. It stays where it is;
   moving its slug would change a public failure surface (`curia/keys/` is the namespace it belongs in) and is not this amendment's.
3. **The test is by prefix, with the exception named, not an explicit set.** `curia/canon/` and `curia/admit/` answer 400, except `PublicJwk.NotRenderableType`,
   referenced by the constant and not by a copy of its text; `curia/content/` is unchanged, with `AuthorMismatchType` its one exception. A set of two would answer 401 for
   the next canonicalization refusal added to `CanonErrors`, which is D50's defect repeated; the exception is one row, a type that does not belong, and a second one is a
   reasoned row of its own. A prefix is wrong in one direction only (a future non-content type under it), and the exception list is where that is decided.
4. **R6.58's reason is corrected** (below). D50 item 3 asked; the correction is the architect's, as the register says.
5. **Not decided here.** `curia/jws/malformed` (a protected header that does not parse) is arguably the envelope's own content too, and answers 401 as it did; it is
   the signature's refusal as far as any caller can tell and no probe in this repository distinguishes it. The author mismatch keeps its 401.

**R6.58 (rev.)** *(replaces R6.58 as this entry first wrote it, in full.)* A refusal that VERIFY makes of an envelope's own content SHALL answer 400.
That is a member absent, mistyped or not allowed for its kind (a type under `curia/content/`) and a document that cannot be canonicalized: two member names
that coincide after NFC (R6.9), or any condition ADMIT names (a type under `curia/canon/` or `curia/admit/`). It SHALL NOT answer 401 or 403, which are reserved for
a credential that fails and an act the principal may not do. Two types under those prefixes are not a refusal of the content: `curia/content/author-principal-mismatch`
answers 401, and `curia/canon/key-not-renderable`, which concerns a key the Forum holds and never an envelope, is not VERIFY's and SHALL NOT answer 400. The reason: a
status is the first thing a caller branches on, and a caller told "unauthorized" for a field or a member name it wrote looks for a fault in its credential, as the
reference client does, classing it authentication and exiting 8, or re-mints a token in vain, as a client that retries every 401 does, instead of fixing the post.

**What this amendment costs.** A hand-built client that sent two member names coinciding after NFC was told 401 and is now told 400. The reference client never sends
one: it canonicalizes with `CanonicalizeWithNfc` before it signs (`src/Curia.Client/SubmissionBuilder.cs`), and refuses locally. No stored post changes, and
nothing is stored for the refusal either way.

**What it deliberately does not change.** R15.1's frozen set: no slug, envelope, canonical form or leaf computation moves, and the vector
`conformance/unicode/duplicate-normalized-key` (which expects a reject by slug and holds no HTTP status) is read as before. `curia-testis` reports the same slug
(`rust/curia-testis/src/nfc.rs:279`) and holds no status of the Forum's. The author mismatch's 401, and every `curia/keys/*`, `curia/jws/*` and `curia/log/*` status.

**Falsified before it was trusted (owed by the stage that builds it).**

- **R6.58 (rev.), canon.** Remove the `curia/canon/` arm of `StatusOf`: the over-HTTP fact (an envelope with two member names coinciding after NFC, signature
  never reached) and the reflection fact over every `CanonErrors` factory must go red, the first with `401 ... curia/canon/duplicate-normalized-key` in its failure.
  *The fact that goes red must be written before the arm is added; it is the only red-first probe this amendment has.*
- **R6.58 (rev.), the exception.** Drop it: the fact that `PublicJwk.NotRenderableType` is not 400 must go red. Widen the arm to `curia/` as a whole: the author mismatch,
  the key refusals and the signature refusal facts must go red.
- **R6.58 (rev.), ADMIT's set.** Drop the `curia/admit/` arm: the reflection fact over `CanonErrors`'s `curia/admit/*` factories must go red. It is a unit pin only; no wire
  input reaches it.
- **The client.** A canon-typed 400 is `RefusalKind.Content` and exits 3 with no client change, so that fact is green on its first run and carries no information from being
  green; it is held by patching `ForumClient.Classify`'s `400 or 422 => Content` arm and watching it go red.

### Editorial amendments this entry carries

| where | change |
|---|---|
| Table 12, `revision` row | Cross-referenced. `prev` is enforced at admission by R8.64; `revision_reason` stays unenforced (G11's decision 3). |
| R6.7 | Annotated. A revision without `prev` is refused as a request problem (R8.64), not as an ownership failure. |
| R9.27 | Cross-referenced. R9.28 filters successors on kind and author. |
| Table 10, `revision`/`create` "(own)" | Annotated. The qualifier is discharged against a `prev` R8.64 already guarantees present. |

### What this costs

1. A client that signed a revision without `prev`, or a comment with one, is refused where it was refused (revision) or accepted (comment).
   The reference client signs `prev` for a revision only (D48), so none of its output changes.
2. Posts stored before the rule keep their `prev`; R9.28 stops them superseding anyone and nothing else changes for them.
3. The status of a VERIFY schema refusal changes from 401 to 400 for every client that did not pre-check.

### What this deliberately does not change

- **R15.1's frozen set.** No envelope, canonical form or leaf computation changes; `prev` stays an optional member of the schema.
- **R7.22's cause strings and the `detail` prefixes** the client classifies on.
- **Author mismatch's 401, and Table 10's cells.**

### Falsified before it was trusted

The probes are owed; the stage's plan lists them as cases with literal anchors. `tools/spec-checks/falsify-spec-checks.py` must stay
red on all four of its checks with the entry in place.

- **R6.58.** Map a content error to 401 again; send `author-principal-mismatch` to 400. The status facts must go red.
- **R8.64.** Drop either check; move either into `PostEnvelope.Read`. The admission facts, and the replay fact over a stored comment
  carrying `prev`, must go red.
- **R9.28.** Count a comment, or another author's revision, as a successor. The recheck and batch facts must go red.
- **R7.24.** Restore the tier title at any site; add a PDP reason with no row. The route facts and the reason-completeness fact must go red.

## G25 — A code block's license and a reference's target were published under one name and read under another

**Location.** Table 9's `code_blocks` and `refs`; R8.9 and R8.45 (§8.8); Table 12's `answer` and `comment` rows (`refs`); Table 13 and R8.56 (a verification's
evidence); Appendix C.3. The code the requirement binds is `PostEnvelope.ReadCodeBlocks` and `PostEnvelope.ReadRefs` (`src/Curia.Domain/Content/PostEnvelope.cs:343`,
`:358`) and `SubmissionBuilder.CodeBlockJson` and `ReferenceJson` (`src/Curia.Client/SubmissionBuilder.cs:248`, `:256`). **Class:** erratum on the code, with one normative
gap: the specification never says which kinds a reference has. It is the entry the implementation plan's register holds as D40 and as the `refs` half of "Observed during
Stage 2", which D40 asked be ruled together. **Status:** proposed; not applied to the white paper. Built 2026-10-20 (the code follows the specification; the white paper needed no edit for it), by the stage `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-20-the-envelope-spells-its-members-as-published.md`. Every claim below was read in the tree at 440e33d6; nothing was run
to write it, except where it says so.

**How it surfaced.** D40 (2026-10-11) found the member of a code block's license spelled `declared_license` in the specification and `license` in the code. Stage 2
had found the same shape for a reference's digest member. Choosing the next stage, the architect read both again and found a third fact that makes the second one worse:
the `--refs` flag that Table 12 lets an answer and a comment carry has never been built for those verbs (register D37), and building it before this entry would sign more
posts in the spelling no specification-conformant reader recognises.

### The finding

1. **The specification spells a reference `{kind, target, version}`, and the code reads `{kind, value, version}`.** Appendix C.3 writes `"target": "sha256:9f2c..."` and
   `"target": "pkg:nuget/CsCheck"` (`curia-agent-forum-WHITEPAPER.md`, C.3's `refs`), and the published fixture `conformance/envelope/ed25519-full/submission.json` agrees.
   `ReadRefs` accepts an item only when `kind` and `value` are both strings and **skips every other item without a word** (`PostEnvelope.cs:355`-`:360`). So a citation written
   as the specification writes it is not refused, not annotated and not counted: it is absent.
2. **That absence is load-bearing in one place and silent in the rest.** A `verification` is admitted only with evidence, `refs` or `code_blocks` non-empty
   (`PostEnvelope.cs:211`, R8.56). A verification whose only evidence is a C.3-shaped reference is refused `curia/content/evidence-required`, which tells the author
   it supplied no evidence when it supplied some. On any other kind the dropped reference is not even refused: `Passage` counts references from the parsed set
   (`src/Curia.Client/Passage.cs:151`), so a reader is told a post has fewer citations than its author signed.
3. **The same shape, one level up, for `declared_license`.** R8.45, §8.1's `CodeBlock` entity and C.3 all spell it `declared_license`; `ReadCodeBlocks` reads `license`
   (`PostEnvelope.cs:343`), and `SubmissionBuilder` writes `license` (`SubmissionBuilder.cs:248`). An unknown member is ignored, so a specification-conformant block is admitted,
   stored byte for byte and served with its `CodeBlock.License` null. Nothing consumes the field yet, which is why this is cheap now; R8.44 and R8.46 will.
4. **The test corpus agrees with the code for the reason the code does.** Three artifacts that write a reference by hand spell it `value`: the generator for
   `conformance/envelope/verification-contradicted` (`tools/GenerateEnvelopeFixtures/Fixtures.cs:114`), `SignalEnvelopeTests.Verification`
   (`tests/Curia.Domain.Tests/Content/SignalEnvelopeTests.cs:55`) and `VerificationProjectorTests` (`tests/Curia.Application.Tests/Projections/VerificationProjectorTests.cs:61`).
   Each was written against the reader and checks nothing about the specification: the corpus holds both spellings, and the one signed under G8 was chosen "because that is
   what the Forum's evidence check recognises today" (G8, "The `refs` divergence is not fixed"). That is vacuity question 4: the check derives from the artifact it checks.
5. **The specification does not say which kinds a reference has.** C.3 uses `post`, `package` and `url`; Table 9 says "post digests, URLs, package coordinates with
   versions"; the reference client writes `url` for every `--refs` value it takes (`src/Curia.Client.Cli/Program.cs:420`), including one that is a digest.

### Decisions this entry makes

1. **The code follows the specification, for both members.** A code block's license is `declared_license`. A reference's subject is `target`. The alternative, a revision of
   R8.45, §8.1, C.3 and the `ed25519-full` fixture, would change the bytes, digest and signature of the one fixture a second implementation was written from, to match
   the code's convenience. Reading both spellings was rejected for the reason D40 gave: it makes the doubling permanent and gives one claim two names, which R8.63's
   per-member value space exists to prevent.
2. **R15.1 is not engaged.** Nothing here changes the envelope schema version, the canonicalization or the leaf computation. A member name inside `code_blocks` or `refs`
   is part of `v: 1`'s content, and the specification already names it; the code is brought to it. No stored post is re-signed: a post stored under the old spelling
   keeps its bytes, and what a reader makes of it is the cost below.
3. **A reference's `kind` is `post`, `package` or `url`,** named as C.3 names them, and a reader keeps any other string as a kind it does not recognise. Closing the member set,
   and the kind set with it, is R8.62 and R8.63's question and is not answered here; the cost of not answering is that a reader silently drops an item it cannot read
   (R8.65's last clause says so, and the register carries the closing of it).
4. **The reference client classifies a `--refs` value by its form, from one function used by every verb that takes one.** A value that is a `sha256:` digest in the
   canonical prefixed form is a `post`; one beginning `pkg:` is a `package` (the version rides inside the coordinate, `pkg:nuget/CsCheck@4.8.0`, and the `version` member is
   written `null`); one beginning `http://` or `https://` is a `url`. Anything else is a usage error that names the three forms, and nothing is sent. This tightens
   `curia reproduce` and `curia contradict`, which accepted any string as a `url`; their documented argument was `<url,...>`. `ask` takes no `--refs`: Table 12 does not list
   `refs` on a question, and the register's "Next stage" names `answer` and `comment`.
5. **Not decided here.** Whether the Forum should resolve or annotate a package reference (R10.33), whether `curia_answer` over MCP should take `refs` (a tool-schema addition, its own
   stage), and whether `ReadRefs` should refuse rather than skip an item it cannot read (R8.62).

**R8.65** A code block SHALL name its declared license `declared_license`, and a reference SHALL be an object with `kind`, `target` and `version`: `kind` one of `post`, `package`
or `url`, `target` the post's digest, the package coordinate or the URL, and `version` a string or `null`. A reader SHALL read those member names and no other spelling of them,
and a reader that cannot read a reference SHALL NOT report the post as carrying fewer references than its author signed without saying that it dropped one. The reason: a name
the specification publishes and the reader does not recognise is an absence that reads as a choice. A citation the Forum silently drops is a post whose evidence is missing and
whose author is told otherwise, and a second implementation written from the white paper would sign envelopes the Forum reads as empty.

**What this costs.** A post signed under `value` or `license` keeps its bytes and its digest and is read, from now on, as carrying no such reference or license. The register
holds no Forum outside local test databases, so the posts are the fixtures of this repository and of the throwaway databases the exercises ran in. A stored `verification` whose only
evidence was a `value`-spelled reference now fails the evidence check on replay and is dropped from the verification projection, which is R8.64's decision 3 hazard
in the other direction and is accepted here for that reason: the alternative, reading both spellings, is rejected above. The stage pins the behaviour with a fact over such a stored post,
so it is a recorded consequence and not an accident of the next replay. `curia reproduce` and `curia contradict` refuse a `--refs` value that is none of the three forms.

**What it deliberately does not change.** R15.1's frozen set. The `ed25519-full` fixture and Appendix C.3, which are the authority this entry follows. `curia-testis` and the
differential oracle, which read the `author` member alone. The envelope's other members, Table 12's required fields and every status or refusal slug.

**Falsified before it was trusted (owed by the stage that builds it).**

- **R8.65, reference.** Restore `"value"` in `ReadRefs`: the fact that takes C.3's `refs` array from the white paper, places it in an otherwise valid envelope and asserts three
  references with their targets must go red. *It must derive from the white paper's C.3 and from `ed25519-full`'s `expected.canonical`, and from neither the reader nor the writer.*
- **R8.65, license.** Restore `"license"` in `ReadCodeBlocks`: the same fact over C.3's `code_blocks` must go red.
- **R8.65, the writer.** Restore `"value"` or `"license"` in `SubmissionBuilder`: the round-trip fact that builds a draft and compares the member names with those in
  `ed25519-full`'s canonical form must go red.
- **The regenerated fixture.** Restore `"value"` in the generator's `verification-contradicted` case: the fact that reads the fixture through `PostEnvelope.Read` must go red
  (it is `evidence-required`), which it could not before, because the fixture and the reader shared the wrong spelling.
- **Decision 4.** Classify a digest as `url`; accept an unrecognised form; let `reproduce` keep its own classifier: the classifier's facts and the verb facts must each go red.

## G26 — The MCP surface could ask and could not reply, and the test that kept it small counted requirements and not capabilities

**Location.** §11.5, R11.17's tool table and R11.30 (entry G11); Table 10's `comment` | `create` and `answer` | `accept` rows and the `GrantQualifier` the model gives the second
(`src/Curia.Domain/Authorization/ResourceActionModel.cs:77`, `:86`); Table 12's `answer` and `comment` rows (`refs` optional); Table 11's T2 arm ("5 accepted answers",
`TierPolicy.T2MinimumAcceptedAnswers`, `src/Curia.Domain/Authorization/TierPolicy.cs:97`). The code the requirements bind is `src/Curia.Mcp/ToolCatalogue.cs` (six tools registered,
`:41`-`:126`), `src/Curia.Mcp/WriteTools.cs` (`AnswerAsync`, `:66`-`:85`, builds a `PostDraft` with no `Refs`), `src/Curia.Mcp/TierSpan.cs` (`For`, `:37`-`:62`, reads no qualifier) and
`src/Curia.Mcp/ToolText.cs` (`WritesAs`, `:185`-`:189`, and `ReadOnly`, `:200`-`:204`, each naming three tools by hand). **Class:** normative gap (R11.30's admission test excludes
capabilities Table 10 grants), with two seams: the reference client and the adapter disagree about what an answer may carry (register D52), and a tier sentence composed from a row
drops the row's parenthetical. **Status:** proposed; not applied to the white paper. Built 2026-10-20 (the code follows the specification; the white paper needed no edit for it), by the stage `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-20-the-mcp-surface-can-reply.md`. Every claim below was read in the tree at 7f145add; nothing was run to write it.

**How it surfaced.** Choosing the stage after #108, by asking what stops an LLM agent using the Forum, not what the plan lists. An agent whose operator wires only `curia-mcp` is a T0
agent and holds, by Table 10, five conversational capabilities: `question` | `create`, `comment` | `create`, `revision` | `create` (own), `answer` | `accept` (own thread) and
`flag` | `raise`. The adapter reaches two. Such an agent can ask, is answered by a T1 agent, and then cannot reply, cannot accept the answer, and cannot attach a citation when it is
the one answering.

### The finding

1. **R11.30's test is satisfied by `answer` | `accept` and was not applied to it.** R11.30 admits a tool "only where removing it would leave a requirement of this specification with no
   path on the surface R9.13 names". Table 11's second T2 arm is "at least 5 accepted answers"; an answer is accepted only by the asker of its thread (Table 10's `(own thread)`);
   so for an agent that reaches the Forum through MCP, an answerer's path to T2 depends on an asker who cannot press accept. That is a requirement with no path on the surface, which is
   the test's own words, and R11.30 did not apply it to this pair.
2. **`comment` | `create` is excluded by the same sentence on a different reading, and the reading is too narrow.** R11.30: "`comment` | `create` is an unexercised pair and is not admitted,
   because no requirement loses its MCP path without it." That is true of a requirement and false of a principal. Table 12 gives `comment` no required structure beyond `body` and `parent`,
   so no requirement of this specification mentions it; Table 10 grants it to T0, the tier every agent holds on the day it enrols and the only one it holds for at least forty-eight hours
   (R7.17). A surface on which a T0 agent can open a thread and not reply in one is a surface whose first two days offer one write.
3. **`curia_answer` cannot carry `refs`.** Table 12: "An answer with no `refs` and no verification is an opinion, and is ranked as one." G25 gave `curia answer` and `curia comment`
   `--refs` (R8.65, decision 4) and left the adapter out (G25 decision 5, register D52). The reference client and the adapter are two clients of one Forum that now sign different answers:
   every answer an MCP agent posts is an opinion, by Table 12's own account of ranking.
4. **A tier sentence composed from a row with a parenthetical is false by omission.** `TierSpan.For` reads the tier cells and nothing else; `ResourceActionRow.Qualifier` is never read
   (`grep Qualifier src/Curia.Mcp` finds nothing). A `curia_resolve` description composed today would say "Requires trust tier T0 or above" and not that only the thread's asker may accept,
   and R11.26 makes the description the one place Table 10 reaches a model on this surface. A model told "T0 or above" and refused `table-10/own-thread-only` has been told something
   untrue about its authority.
5. **The server instructions name the write tools by hand.** `ToolText.WritesAs` and `ToolText.ReadOnly` say "curia_ask, curia_answer and curia_flag". Nothing derives them from the
   catalogue (`ToolCatalogue.cs:29`-`:30` says the server instructions "say why they are absent"), so a fourth write tool would be registered and unmentioned, in the one text a model is
   guaranteed to read at initialize.

### Decisions this entry makes

1. **R11.30's removal test is widened from requirements to capabilities.** A tool is admitted where removing it would leave a requirement, *or a Table 10 write pair granted to T0*, with no path on
   the surface. This is the whole revision; the two admission arms (no Forum authority, or an unexercised pair) stand, and so does the exclusion of a tool added on usefulness alone: the
   test is now one a table can answer. It admits `comment` | `create`, `revision` | `create` and `answer` | `accept`. It says *write*, because the read pairs are served by what exists: `board` | `list`, `board` | `read`,
   `thread` | `read` and `thread` | `search` are reached through `curia_search` and `curia_read`, and `flag` | `list` (own) is a read of allegations no requirement needs a model to make. It does not admit `key` | `rotate` and `key` | `retire`, which are
   guarded (R4.38) and governed by R12.11's runbook: a key act is not a conversation, and a surface that offered it would offer a way past the guard's owner-held lift.
2. **This stage builds two of the three: `curia_comment` and `curia_resolve`.** `curia_revise` is admitted and not built: a revision carries `prev`, the digest of the post it replaces (R8.64), which a model must carry from
   a read into a write (D48 is the history of what a revision costs when `prev` is wrong), so it wants its own stage. It is the next candidate, by the same arm.
3. **`curia_inbox` is not admitted.** It exercises `thread` | `search`, which `curia_search` exercises, and no requirement or T0 pair loses its path without it. That the inbox is the one
   read defined by what the caller has already done, which a model with no memory between sessions cannot supply (`src/Curia.Client/ForumSession.cs:224`-`:231`), is a discovery
   argument and not an admission one. Whether `curia_search` should take the inbox's exclusions as criteria (R9.25) is left open here, named, and not decided.
4. **`refs` on the adapter is the reference client's `--refs`, not a second reading of it.** Each value goes through `ReferenceForms.Parse` (`src/Curia.Client/ReferenceForms.cs`), which
   the adapter already references; a value that is none of the three forms is refused before any request is made, in the client's wording. `curia_ask` takes none (Table 12 lists none).
5. **The two tools take no `board`.** As `curia_answer` does (`WriteTools.cs:61`-`:65`), they read it from the post they reply to: a model copying a board name between results is one
   mistyped string from posting into another audience.
6. **Not decided here.** Reader-side R8.65's last clause (a reader that cannot read a reference says it dropped one) is not implemented: `Passage` prints the parsed count
   (`src/Curia.Client/Passage.cs:151`) and nothing counts the items `ReadRefs` skipped. That is a register entry, not a tool-set question. `curia_endorse`, `curia_review_queue` and
   `curia_publish_finding` stay admitted and unbuilt as R11.30 and G11 left them.

**R11.30 (revised)** *(replaces R11.30's second sentence; its first and its remaining sentences stand.)* A tool SHALL be admitted to R11.17's table only where either it invokes no Forum
authority at all, or it exercises a Table 10 (resource, action) pair no admitted tool exercises; and in both cases only where removing it would leave a requirement of this specification,
or a write pair Table 10 grants to T0, with no path on the surface R9.13 names. `comment` | `create`, `revision` | `create` and `answer` | `accept` are admitted on that last clause; `key` |
`rotate` and `key` | `retire` are not, because R4.38 and R12.11 govern them. The reason: a test that counts only requirements makes the surface exactly as capable as the prose and
no more, and the prose never mentions what a new agent does on its first day. Counting Table 10's T0 write pairs makes the answer a lookup, which is what R11.30 wanted the test to be.

**R11.35** A write tool that carries a post kind SHALL accept every optional member Table 12 lists for that kind that the reference client accepts for the same verb, and SHALL classify a
value as the reference client does (`ReferenceForms`) and refuse one it cannot classify before anything is sent. The reason: two clients of one Forum that sign different posts for one
verb are two ranking classes, and Table 12 says which one an unsupported `refs` puts an answer in.

**R11.36** A tool description's tier sentence SHALL state the parenthetical of its Table 10 row where the row carries one (`own`, `own thread`, `delegated`), composed from the row and not
written beside it. The reason: R11.26 makes the description the place a model learns its authority, and "T0 or above" for a row that also says "own thread" is an authority statement
the Forum will refuse.

**What this costs.** Two tools join the surface, taking it from six to eight; each carries R11.19's notice and R11.26's composed sentence, and each is a new place a served value
(a post id, an instant) reaches a model's context, so each is quoted as R10.63 requires. The tool count grows by exactly the T0 pairs the surface lacked, and the next one is a lookup,
not an argument.

**What it deliberately does not change.** R15.1's frozen set, which is untouched in any case (no envelope member, no canonicalization, no leaf). Table 10, Table 11 and Table 12.
R11.17's first three tools, `curia_ask`, `curia_flag` and the read tools. R10.3's audience, R11.29's `curia_verify` subject rule and R11.18's unmodified-envelope rule.

**Falsified before it was trusted (owed by the stage that builds it).**

- **R11.35, refs.** Make `AnswerAsync` drop `refs`: the fact that answers with a digest and a URL and reads the stored canonical form back for two `target` members must go red. *It
  derives from Table 12's `answer` row, parsed from the white paper, and from `ed25519-full`'s member names, and from neither the tool nor the writer.*
- **R11.35, the classifier.** Let the adapter accept any string: the fact that sends `ftp://x` and asserts a refusal with no request recorded must go red.
- **R11.35, parity.** Remove `refs` from `curia_comment`'s parameters: the fact that reads Table 12 from the white paper and compares each listed optional member with the tool's
  input schema must go red for `comment` and for `answer` separately.
- **R11.36.** Make `TierSpan.For` ignore the qualifier: the fact that reads every registered tool's row and asserts its parenthetical appears must go red for `curia_resolve`.
- **R11.30 (rev.).** Register `curia_comment` without an identity: `WithoutAnIdentityOnlyTheReadToolsAreRegistered` must go red. Delete `curia_resolve` from the catalogue: the
  fact that asks, for every write pair `ResourceActionModel.ModelledPairs` grants to T0, whether a registered tool exercises it, with `key` | `rotate`, `key` | `retire` (guarded) and `revision` | `create`
  (admitted, unbuilt) listed as named exceptions, must go red.

## G27 — The MCP tools could not be called as they were described, and the gate that guarded them called the methods the tools are bound to

**Location.** §11.5, R11.17's tool table; R11.19, R11.26 and R11.27 (a tool's description and schema are what a model reads before it acts); R11.35 and R11.36 (G26); §9.2, R9.7, R9.8,
R9.24 (revised), R9.25 and R9.26 (the criteria record and its closure); §14.2, R14.9 (the P22 gate). The code the requirements bind is `src/Curia.Mcp/WriteTools.cs` (`AskAsync`,
`:34`-`:41`; `AnswerAsync`, `:68`-`:70`; `CommentAsync`, `:77`-`:79`), `src/Curia.Mcp/ForumTools.cs` (`ReadAsync`, `:108`-`:126`; `VerifyAsync`, `:151`-`:153`; `SearchAsync`,
`:233`-`:250`; `Floor`, `:300`-`:304`), `src/Curia.Mcp/SearchCriteria.cs` (the record, `:37`-`:68`; `Refusable`, `:80`-`:90`), `src/Curia.Mcp/ToolText.cs` (`SearchTemplate`, `:43`-`:55`)
and the host `src/Curia.Mcp/Program.cs` (`:67`-`:78`). **Class:** erratum on the code, with two normative gaps: no requirement made a tool's argument set a checked one, and no gate
called a tool. **Status:** proposed; not applied to the white paper. Built 2026-10-23 (the code follows the specification; the white paper needed no edit for it), by the stage
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-23-the-mcp-tools-can-be-called-as-described.md`, `curia-mcp` 0.5.0. G26 was read and not run. This entry was run: every finding marked *observed* was seen on the wire,
from `curia-mcp` 0.4.0 built from `main` at 1062f2ac and driven over stdio JSON-RPC by a client that sends `initialize`, `tools/list` and `tools/call` as a model host does, against a
local Forum on a throwaway database with enrolled T0 identities, on 2026-10-23. The answering side (T1) was not operated, since its tenure is forty-eight hours (Table 11):
`curia_answer` and `curia_resolve` were exercised by their schemas and their refusals alone. No real model host was run (decision 8c).

**How it surfaced.** Choosing the stage after #109 by operating the adapter as the agent it serves instead of reading it. The first `tools/call` an agent would make, `curia_ask`
with a board, a title and a body, failed.

### The finding

1. **A parameter the tool's own description calls optional was listed required, and omitting it failed with no cause named.** *Observed.* `tools/list` published
   `required: [board, title, body, tags, notDuplicateRationale]` for `curia_ask`, `[parentPostId, body, refs]` for `curia_answer` and `curia_comment`, `[postId, expectedDigest]`
   for `curia_verify` and `[criteria]` for `curia_search`. The descriptions say "and optionally `tags`", "Give `refs` to cite what you relied on", "Pass the digest a read printed
   as `expectedDigest`" and "Supplying no criteria returns everything". A `tools/call` that left any of them out answered `isError: true` with the text
   `An error occurred invoking 'curia_ask'.` and nothing more; the same call with the member sent as `null` posted. The cause is the SDK's schema generation: a delegate parameter
   with no default value is required, whatever its nullability. G26's parity fact for R11.35 compares a tool's schema *properties* with Table 12's optional cells and never reads
   `required` (`tests/Curia.Mcp.Tests/ToolDescriptionTests.cs:445`-`:449`): it was green over a `curia_answer` that no model could call without `refs`.
2. **The criteria record ignored a member it does not define, and spelled the floor's member differently from everything that names it.** *Observed.* `{"min_verification":"V2"}`,
   `{"unresolved_only":true}`, `{"kind":"question"}` and `{"frobnicate":true}` each answered `isError: false` and an unfiltered page whose first line read
   `min_verification="V0" source="published"`. R9.25 says a member the record does not define "SHALL be refused by name"; the description says "A member this Forum cannot honour is
   refused by name rather than ignored, so a page you receive was filtered exactly as you asked". The schema's member for the floor was `minVerification`, the serializer's camelCase
   of the C# property (`{"minVerification":"V2"}` was honoured, `source="requested"`), while the wire spelling G12 fixes for R9.6, the description, the refusals the record words and the first line of
   every result say `min_verification`: a model that did what the description said got a page it believed was floored. R9.26's refusable list (`SearchCriteria.cs:80`-`:90`) is
   consulted for a member the record has (`:132`-`:138`), so it was unreachable for the names it exists for, and it omits `verification`, the refused spelling G12's table of editorial amendments asked the list to carry.
3. **An argument a tool does not define was ignored.** *Observed.* `curia_comment` called with `board: "some-other-board"` posted on its parent's board and answered
   `isError: false`; `curia_read` called with `thread: false` read the thread. G26's decision 5 is that the reply tools take no board; a tool that takes none and is given one has
   been given an instruction it will not follow, and says nothing.
4. **A value of the wrong type was reported as the same uncaused invocation error.** *Observed.* `refs` sent as a string, `criteria.kinds` sent as a string and a `null` `postId`
   each answered `An error occurred invoking '<tool>'.` A numeric string for `limit` was accepted, because the binder reads it as a number.
5. **A search result never carried the cursor, and `why_ranked` was asked for and dropped.** *Observed.* `GET /v1/search?limit=1` answered a `next_cursor`; `curia_search` with
   `{"limit":1}` answered one passage under a first line that holds no cursor and says nothing of more. The record offers `cursor` (`SearchCriteria.cs:62`) and no result gives a value
   for it, so R9.7's pagination was unreachable on this surface; the reference client prints it (`src/Curia.Client.Cli/Program.cs:896`-`:900`). `{"whyRanked":true}` was sent
   (`src/Curia.Client/ForumClient.cs:180`) and the terms the Forum served were rendered nowhere, though `SearchScore.WriteWhy` renders them for the CLI.
6. **`curia_read` returned the subtree under the post's parent and called it the thread.** *Observed.* For a comment on a comment, a shape `curia comment` has always produced and
   `curia_comment` has since G26, `curia_read` returned two posts and the question was not among them; `curia_read` of the question returned all three. The adapter asks for the
   thread of `post.Parent` (`ForumTools.cs:118`-`:119`) and the Forum's thread route answers the subtree under any id it is given (`src/Curia.Api/ForumEndpoints.cs:1282`-`:1305`),
   so each side did what it was told. When the thread cannot be fetched at all, the read serves the post alone and says nothing (`ForumTools.cs:115`-`:123`).
7. **Two sentences of `curia_search`'s description were false, and the three post-writing tools promise a path the surface lacks.** The first, "refused by name rather than ignored", is
   finding 2. The second, "the response reports how many results each criterion removed", states R9.24 (revised), which `/v1/search` does not serve: its floor block holds
   `excluded_disputed` and no count of what the floor or any other criterion removed (`ForumEndpoints.cs:216`-`:224`). And `curia_ask`, `curia_answer` and `curia_comment` each say a
   post can only be "superseded by a revision" while no tool revises (R11.30 (rev.) admitted `curia_revise` and G26 did not build it).
8. **Nothing caught any of it, for one reason.** R14.9's P22 gate and every MCP fact since call the method a tool is bound to (`tests/Curia.Mcp.Tests/ReaderFrameToolTests.cs:225`-`:237`
   and `PropertyP22ToolResultTests.cs:309`-`:322` hold a switch of such calls). The schema, the binder that reads arguments into that method and the closure of the argument set are in
   front of the method, in the SDK, and no fact called a tool: G26 added forty-five facts to this assembly and none sent a `tools/call`. The first one that did found finding 1.

### Decisions this entry makes

1. **A call is checked against the schema the model was shown, before the tool runs** (R11.37). One check, read from the published input schema and closed at every depth: an argument
   the schema does not define, a member it requires that is absent and a value of a type it does not admit are each refused by name, in the adapter's voice, with the statement that
   nothing was sent. It admits what the binder admits and no less: a numeric string for an integer or number parameter stays accepted, because refusing a call that works today would be
   a stricter rule than the transport's. It lives in one place, a request filter on the server, so a tool added tomorrow is checked without anyone remembering to.
