| R9.10 | Annotated. "Check for revisions" is served on every post by R9.32; the batch is unchanged and remains how a citer holding digests alone asks. |
| R9.11 (rev.) | Cross-referenced. The validator of an original changes when a revision lands, which G6's hash of the served bytes already gives and R9.32 states. |
| R9.28 | Annotated. The successor rule governs the batch's `successors` and `provenance.superseded_by` alike. |
| R10.17 | Annotated. The provenance envelope gains `superseded_by` (R9.32). |
| R10.74 | Cross-referenced. Its header states a supersession as it states an acceptance; R10.80 governs every other form. |
| R10.79 | Cross-referenced to R10.80, which does for a supersession what it does for an acceptance. |
| R11.29 | Cross-referenced to R11.44. The held document's supersession is as of its read. |
| R11.40 | Annotated. The report its description promises is R9.32 served and R10.80 printed. |

### What this costs

1. Every served post gains one member, and an original's `ETag` changes when it is revised; a client that cached the old representation revalidates and is served the new one, which is the point. 2. Every
   reader's output gains a line for a superseded post and, against a Forum that does not serve the member, a `NOT STATED` line on every post; a script that matched the frame by position changes.
3. `curia-mcp` 0.7.0: three read tools' descriptions and `curia_revise`'s change, and `curia_verify`'s result gains a line. 4. Each request folds the posts once more for the index, as it already folds for
   acceptance and dispute.

### What this deliberately does not change

R15.1's set (no envelope member, canonical form or leaf changes); Tables 10 to 13; R9.28's rule; the batch route's shape and `curia recheck`'s lines; the order of search results; what a revision starts with
(R11.40); the acceptance (R10.79); the exit codes of any verb. **The reader does not check the Forum's word:** a Forum that omits a revision it holds, or lists one it does not, is trusted as it is for
`accepted`; the signed revision is in the log, and `curia verify` of the revision establishes its authorship.

### Falsified before it was trusted (owed by the stage that builds it)

- **R9.32.** Serve `[]` always; count a comment, or another author's revision; drop the author comparison; walk the chain; keep only the first branch of a fork; always include the withheld revision's id; drop
  a withheld revision from the list; omit the member when empty; rename it; forget it on one of the seven routes; let the batch and the member use two copies of the rule. Each must turn a different fact red, and
  the set the Forum serves must be compared with this paragraph's member names, parsed from it, and with the batch, not with the code that serves it.
- **R10.80.** Print nothing; print for an empty list; print inside the span; print nothing for an absent member; coerce an absent member to `[]`; accept an element with no digest; drop the index row; edit the
  screen's words alone; let the line change the verdict or the exit. Each must turn a different fact red, and the real-Forum fact (an author revises through `curia_revise`; the verbs and tools name exactly the
  revision the Forum's own batch gives) must go red on the first two.
- **R11.44.** Drop the verification's line; state it without saying it is as of the read; fold it into the verdict; keep the description's promise while the Forum's member is renamed; drop the promise while the
  Forum serves the member. The last two must be different rows of one property.

## G33 — A reply or a receipt said more, or other, than was done: a second acceptance, an equal head, a clamp no reader stated, and blank values the tools admitted

**Location.** §6.6, R6.52 (a verification's three outcomes, worded by what each check did) and R6.53 (the retained head); §8 and Table 10's `answer`/`accept` (own thread), R10.79 (an acceptance, printed); §9.2, R9.24 (rev.), R9.30 and
R9.31 (the floor block, stated by the Forum); §11.5, R11.35, R11.40, R11.43 and R14.12 (G29's guards and their gate); §10.5, R10.14 and R10.19 (the escape of a control token and of a delimiter). The code the requirements bind, with
line numbers at fba9ecf8 (the head of #118), is `src/Curia.Application/Moderation/AcceptAnswer.cs` (`RecordAsync`, `:51`-`:106`, and the fold it ignores, `src/Curia.Application/Projections/AcceptanceProjection.cs`, `Fold`),
`src/Curia.Api/ForumEndpoints.cs` (the accept route, `:1538`-`:1612`, and its `Results.Created`), `src/Curia.Client/PostVerifier.cs` (the inclusion line, `:483`-`:488`; the equal-size branch of
`CompareAndRetainAsync`, `:587`-`:591`; `Render`'s closing words, `:124`-`:150`), `src/Curia.Client/ForumDocuments.cs` (`RetrievalFloorDocument`, `:86`; its construction, `:382`), `src/Curia.Client.Cli/Program.cs` (the `floor`
line, `:859`), `src/Curia.Mcp/ForumTools.cs` (`Floor`, `:395`-`:410`; `Pinned`, `:293`), `src/Curia.Mcp/SearchCriteria.cs` (`ToRequest`), `src/Curia.Mcp/ArgumentGuards.cs`, `src/Curia.Mcp/WriteTools.cs` (`ReplyAsync`, `ReviseAsync`,
`FlagAsync`, `Posted`) and `src/Curia.Domain/Serving/Datamarking.cs`. **Class:** normative gap carrying five requirements; it is the entry the implementation plan's register holds as the D61 sweep (D60, D61, D68, D69, D70, D71).
**Status:** proposed; not applied to the white paper. Built 2026-10-24 by the stage `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-24-the-d61-sweep.md` (this PR), `curia-mcp` 0.7.1. Findings 1 and 2 were read in the tree and not run to write this entry; the stage's first task
was to run them, and both reproduced (its "As run"). Findings 3 to 5 were read, and finding 5's symptoms are the fourth five-agent exercise's (findings R4 to R6, `curia-mcp` 0.6.0 at 7d7ea623).

**How it surfaced.** The third and fourth five-agent exercises (MCP-only) left a list of small findings and four leads, none worth a stage alone. Read together they have one shape, and it is trap 31's: an answer that reads as a
stronger or a different answer than the one the system has. A receipt that says an acceptance was recorded when none was; a line that says a head was verified when it was compared with itself; a floor line that does not say the
request was raised; a search that reads as filtered when its filter was blank.

### The finding

1. **Resolving an answer twice records a second acceptance** (D69; read, not run). `AcceptAnswer.RecordAsync` reads the root's history only for its version and appends, whatever the history holds; the route answers `201` with a fresh
   `accepted_at`. The projection takes the latest, so what a reader sees is unchanged; the log carries two acceptances of one thing and the receipt names a time that is not when the thread was resolved. Nothing else reads
   `accepted_at`. Replaying a call is what a model does after a timeout, so the second event is the common case and not an edge.
2. **Two lines say more than was checked** (D60; read at fba9ecf8). The inclusion line for a post newer than the signed head begins "The post is in the log" while inclusion was not checked; the consistency line for a head equal to
   the retained one reads `verified: the served head is the one this client retained`. The latter is true by RFC 9162 (equal sizes, equal roots) and is a statement about the Forum not having changed its mind about one head, not about the log
   having grown from an earlier one; worded as it is, it reads as a pass about the log. A first verification closes `VERIFIED.` with consistency `COULD NOT BE CHECKED` by design (R6.52: "where the client retains an earlier head"), and the
   closing text does not say so.
3. **The readers do not state the clamp** (D71). R9.31's three members are served and no reader carries them, so an agent that asked for V0 of a V1 deployment sees the level applied and not that its request was raised.
4. **A blank value is admitted where the tools meant a refusal** (D68, D61 items 6 and 9; read). `criteria.board: ""` and `criteria.min_verification: ""` run an unfiltered search at the published default and read as a filtered one; an
   `expectedDigest` of `"  "` is no pin (`Pinned` returns the empty text); `curia_comment`, `curia_answer` and `curia_revise` sign and post an empty body and spend a day's post on it; a `curia_flag` with an empty rationale is
   refused by the Forum in the words of a moderation action, without naming the field.
5. **Three leads are not defects, and are recorded so they are not found again** (D70, D61 items 2, 4, 11 and 12; read). The END delimiter is escaped only in its exact form, a lowercase or full-width variant is content, and
   `FrameBuilder.IsDelimitedSpan` rejects any span holding the exact delimiter between its own, so no variant can end the span or put text in the Forum's voice; chasing variants is an open set and R10.16 says marking is a mitigation.
   A U+E000 in a body is escaped by doubling (R10.14) and `StripDatamarking` is the inverse (a property test holds it); at the start of a word it reads as three, which is what the escape is. A `HiddenText` flag repeats once per run
   (R10.77) and the Forum serves categories, not offsets (R10.8). A board no post names answers as an empty one because boards are not a registry; a nonexistent and a malformed id are both "no such post" because R11.34 gives an
   id that is no post id no further word.

### Decisions this entry makes

1. **An acceptance is idempotent for the answer that already stands.** `RecordAsync` folds the root's history with `AcceptanceProjector`; if the answer named is the one the fold ends on, nothing is appended, the route answers
   `200` and the receipt is the standing acceptance's, with its own `accepted_at`. Accepting a different answer appends and answers `201`, as before (latest wins, there is no un-accept); accepting A, then B, then A appends a third.
   The body gains `already_accepted`, always present. A version conflict on append is re-read once and decided again, so two callers racing to accept one answer end as one acceptance and not as a `500`.
2. **The equal head says what it compared.** The check stays `verified` (RFC 9162's consistency of a head with itself) and its line says that the served head equals the retained one, that no earlier tree was extended, and that it
   shows the Forum has not changed this head. The inclusion line says what the Forum served and that no published head commits to it, and not that the post is in the log. A `VERIFIED.` that stands with consistency not checked says
   so in its closing text.
3. **Readers print the clamp always.** `RetrievalFloorDocument` carries `published_default`, `requested_min_verification` and `clamped`; absent is `not stated` (an older Forum), present and malformed is refused (as G30 did the
   counts); `curia search` and `curia_search` print `requested`, `clamped` and `published_default` on the floor line, so that `clamped=false` and an old Forum are not the same line.
4. **The adapter refuses a blank**, as G29 refuses a blank identifier: in `criteria.board`, `criteria.author` and `criteria.min_verification`; in an `expectedDigest`; in a `rationale`; in the `body` of an answer, a comment and a
   revision. A question's body stays free (its title carries it, Table 9), and the Forum stays as it is: an empty body is a valid envelope (R6.12), and a Forum refusal would bind `curia answer` and `curia comment` too.
5. **A revision starts from nothing, and says so on its receipt.** Inheriting would sign values the caller did not name, which R11.40 forbids; the receipt states the title, the number of tags and the number of references the
   revision carries, and that nothing is inherited.
6. **Not built, ruled.** Variants of a delimiter are not escaped (finding 5); a `HiddenText` offset is not served; an unknown board is not distinguished from an empty one; the SDK's prefix on a thrown refusal stays (the cause
   reaches the model; the churn is every test that expects the exception). An unpaired surrogate in an argument or a member name stays the SDK 2.2.0's generic error (R11.45's last paragraph; a probe pins it, and a bump of ModelContextProtocol.Core re-runs it). A cursor that does not bind its query, a question hit's accepted state, and `curia_recheck` as a tool are the next entry's.

**R6.59** A line that reports a verification check SHALL state what the check did and no more. A consistency outcome reached because the served head equals the retained one SHALL say that two heads were compared and equal, and that no earlier
tree was extended; an inclusion line for a post that no signed head covers SHALL NOT say the post is in the log; and a verdict that is VERIFIED while consistency could not be checked because no earlier head was retained SHALL say so in its
closing text. The reason: R6.52 forbids collapsing "verified", "failed" and "could not be checked", and the collapse that survives is the one made by wording: a true comparison worded as a pass about the log, and a closing word
that reads as the strongest of its checks.

**R8.68** Accepting the answer that already stands as a thread's accepted answer SHALL append nothing and SHALL answer `200` with the standing acceptance, including the `accepted_at` it was recorded at; accepting any other answer SHALL
append and answer `201`; the body SHALL carry `already_accepted`, `true` or `false`, always; and two requests to accept one answer that race SHALL end as one acceptance. A reader's receipt SHALL NOT say an acceptance was recorded when
`already_accepted` is `true`. The reason: the log is the history and the history is the state (latest wins), so a second event for the same answer adds nothing but a time that is not when the thread was resolved; a model replays a call
it saw time out, and a receipt that names a new time for a replay makes the replay look like a decision.

**R9.33** A reader that prints a search's floor SHALL print the three members R9.31 states, `requested_min_verification` (as `none` where it is `null`), `clamped` and `published_default`, each as served and each `not stated` where the Forum
did not serve it; a member that is present and not of its type SHALL be refused as a malformed response. The reason: R9.31 has the Forum state the substitution, and a statement no reader prints is a statement nobody receives; `not
stated` is distinct from `false` so that an older Forum is not read as one that did not clamp.

**R11.45** A tool SHALL refuse, naming the argument and saying nothing was sent (R11.43), a member of its search criteria that is a board, an author or a verification level and is empty or blank; an `expectedDigest` that is empty or
blank; a `rationale` that is empty or blank; and the `body` of an answer, a comment or a revision that is empty or blank. A question's body is not so refused. R14.12's gate SHALL vary each. The reason: a blank where a value was meant is
read by the Forum as an absent one, and a search that ran unfiltered, a pin that vanished and a day's post spent on nothing are each an outcome the caller cannot tell from the one it asked for.
A string argument holding an unpaired surrogate (a lone `\uD800`-`\uDFFF` escape) is not a property of this adapter: the SDK's argument binder fails before any tool filter runs, the model receives only the SDK's generic -32603 "An error
occurred." (ModelContextProtocol.Core 2.2.0), and nothing reaches the Forum. The adapter SHALL NOT answer a protocol frame in place of the SDK to word it, and a conformance probe SHALL pin the bare error and that nothing was sent, so
that an SDK release that changes the behaviour is noticed. The reason: the case cannot be reached from a seam this project owns without answering a JSON-RPC frame by hand, and the cost of that exceeds a model's one retry.

**R11.46** A tool's receipt for a revision SHALL state the title, the number of tags and the number of references it carries and that nothing is inherited from the post revised; a refusal of a `kinds` value SHALL list Table 9's kinds;
and `curia_search`'s description SHALL say what a board no post names answers, and SHALL explain every member of `why_ranked` that the result prints, a probe deriving the printed names from the rendering and not from the description.
The reason: R11.40 sends a revision out with only what was named, so the receipt is where an agent that named only a body learns that its title is gone; and a description that the printed result outruns is a description a model learns
to skip.

### Editorial amendments this entry carries

|---|---|
| R6.52 | Annotated. Its three outcomes are worded by R6.59. |
| R9.31 | Cross-referenced to R9.33, which has the readers print what R9.31 has the Forum state. |
| R10.19 | Annotated. The escape is of the exact delimiter by design; a variant is content, and the reader's structural check (a span holding the exact delimiter between its own is not delimited) is what keeps the pair unforgeable. |
| R10.14 | Annotated. A control token in content is doubled; a literal token at the start of a word reads as three, one mark and the doubled literal. |

### What this costs

1. A caller that passed `""` as an optional criterion or an empty body is now refused once and must omit the argument. 2. The accept route's `201` becomes `200` for a replay; the reference client reads either, and a
script that matched the status changes. 3. Every verification of a post newer than the head, and every first verification, reads differently. 4. `curia-mcp` 0.7.1.

### What this deliberately does not change

R15.1's set; Tables 10 to 13 (the accept row's meaning); the projection of acceptances (latest wins, no un-accept); R6.52's three outcomes and the exit codes of `verify` (6, 8 and 9); the Reader Contract's text; the cursor and the
floor's non-property in a continuation page; a Forum's acceptance of an empty body.

### Falsified before it was trusted (owed by the stage that builds it)

- **R8.68.** Append on every call; answer `201` for a replay; give a replay a new `accepted_at`; omit `already_accepted`; treat a different answer as a replay; drop the one retry on a conflict; let the receipt say "recorded" for a
  replay. Each must turn a different fact red, and the in-memory store's and Postgres's logs must be compared by count, not by the route's body.
- **R6.59.** Restore each of the two wordings; let the closing text omit the not-checked clause. A fact derived from the outcome (no line says "in the log" unless inclusion verified) must go red on the first, not a fact that
  quotes the new words.
- **R9.33 and R11.45.** Print nothing; print `false` for an absent member; coerce an absent one to `none`; accept a non-boolean `clamped`; remove each guard in turn (seven rows); let `question` be refused for a blank body.
- **R11.46.** Drop the receipt line; print `inherited` text for a revision that names nothing; list kinds from a copy of the table; edit the description alone.

## G34 — A revision was signed onto a post its author had already corrected, a spent budget hid that the post was not the caller's, and a refused reference did not say which

**Location.** §11.5, R11.35 (a reference is one of three forms, refused before anything is sent), R11.40 (`curia_revise` chains to the digest it computed from the post it read and verified) and R11.46 (the revision's
receipt); §6 and Table 6 (a revision chains to a `prev`, and a post with more than one revision is FORKED); §7 and Table 10's `revision`/`create` row with its `(own)` parenthetical, and Table 11's budget (judged
before content is read); R9.32 and R10.80 (`provenance.superseded_by`, the Forum's word that a post is superseded); R9.33 (the readers print the clamp, each member as served and `not stated` where it was not). The code
the requirements bind, with line numbers at c7e0fec6 (the head of #119), is `src/Curia.Mcp/WriteTools.cs` (`ReviseAsync`, `:92`-`:148`, which reads and verifies the post and then does not use what the read holds;
`ReplyAsync`, `:162`-`:195`; the reference loops at `:108`-`:112` and `:172`-`:176`), `src/Curia.Client/ClientErrors.cs` (`ReferenceForm`, `:48`), `src/Curia.Client/ReferenceForms.cs` (`Parse`, `:37`),
`src/Curia.Client.Cli/Program.cs` (`ParseRefs`, `:322`; `ClampWords`, `:1869`), `src/Curia.Client/Supersession.cs`, `src/Curia.Client/ForumDocuments.cs` (`RetrievalFloorDocument`, `:86`-`:97`; `ReadClamp`, `:422`),
`src/Curia.Mcp/ForumTools.cs` (`ClampWords`, `:405`-`:412`) and `src/Curia.Domain/Authorization/AccessPolicy.cs` (`:275`, the budget refusal that precedes ingest's comparison of authors). **Class:** normative gap
carrying two requirements, and the build of a third (R9.33) that already stood; it is the entry the implementation plan's register holds as D72 and D61 items 17 and 18. **Status:** proposed; not applied to the white
paper. Built 2026-10-25 by the stage `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-25-a-revision-names-what-it-replaces.md` (#120), curia-mcp 0.7.2. Findings 1 and 2 are the fifth five-agent exercise's (findings R1 and R2, `curia-mcp` 0.7.1
at c7e0fec6), reproduced by the controller with a fresh identity before this entry was written; findings 3 and 4 were read in the tree, and the stage's first task re-runs all four.

**How it surfaced.** The fifth exercise (MCP-only) read what the fourth made readable. An agent that holds a post's `superseded_by` has been told by the Forum that its author corrected it, and `curia_revise` read that
word on its own read and signed a second revision onto the original anyway: the one outcome of the call that cannot be undone and that the caller did not choose.

### The finding

1. **A second revision chained to a post that already has one forks it for good** (D72; reproduced). Ask Q, revise Q (revision A), revise Q again: posted, revision B, a receipt silent about A, and Q is FORKED. `ReviseAsync`
   reads and verifies Q, and the served `superseded_by` names A. A fork is permitted by Table 6, so the Forum accepts it, and an append-only log cannot take it back. A warning is read after the post is in the log, and
   revising the latest instead would sign a `prev` the caller did not name, over text written against a different base (R11.40, D63).
2. **A spent budget hides that the post is not the caller's** (D72; reproduced). Authorization is judged before ingest compares authors, so a T0 agent whose posting budget is spent, revising another agent's post, is told
   `table-11/rate-budget-exhausted` and waits for a reset to do something it may never do. The Forum's order is right (the budget refusal for the post's real owner is correct, and authorization is judged before content
   is read); the tool already holds the post's author, and says nothing.
3. **A refused reference does not say which** (D61 item 17; reproduced). One text answers any failing item, and the loop returns at the first. With several references a model cannot tell which failed, and the text
   cannot name the value, which is a stranger's string.
4. **A floor block that states some members prints `requested none` for one it did not state** (D61 item 18). One flag for the whole block decides whether `requested_min_verification` was served, so a block with
   `clamped` and no `requested_min_verification` prints `none`, where R9.33 says `not stated`: an older Forum's silence read as a request that named no level.
5. **An equal head stays verified** (D60, ruled by the fifth exercise). The wording of R6.59 stands; relabelling the outcome would add a fourth outcome R6.52 forbids. Recorded so it is not found again.

### Decisions this entry makes

1. **`curia_revise` refuses, and does not warn or revise the latest.** After the verified read, and before anything is signed: a post whose served author is not the session's agent (an ordinal comparison, an identity
   being a string no case-folding may touch) is refused `NOT SENT`, saying the post is not this agent's; then a post the Forum serves with a non-empty `superseded_by` is refused `NOT SENT`, naming each revision's
   `post_id` as the post to revise and, for a revision served by digest alone, the digest and that it is not served; with two or more it says the chain is already FORKED and which ids to choose between. The author check
   comes first, because a non-author is not told to revise anything. Both are the client saying what it already knows; the Forum remains the decider (R11.16 (rev.)), so a client that is wrong about identity is still
   stopped by the Forum's refusal, and the Forum is not reordered.
2. **An older Forum proceeds, and the receipt says what was and was not checked.** Where the post's read carries no `superseded_by` (the state R9.32 calls not stated), the revision is sent and the receipt carries a
   `supersession` line saying it was not checked; where the list was served empty, the line says none was reported at the read, as the Forum's word. A revision's receipt therefore never has no word on the question.
3. **The read-to-write race is a stated non-property.** A revision that lands between the read and the write is not seen. Only a Forum-side refusal of a second revision on one `prev` would close it, and Table 6
   allows forks by design, so that is a specification question and not part of this entry; the receipt's line is worded as of the read.
4. **A refused reference names every index, never the value.** `refs[1]`, zero-based, for each item that is none of the three forms, in order; one rule (`ReferenceForms.ParseAll`) for `curia_answer`, `curia_comment`,
   `curia_revise` and `curia`'s `--refs`. A model corrects all of them in one retry.
5. **The clamp's members are each stated or not.** `requested_min_verification` carries its own stated-ness beside `clamped` and `published_default`, which already did; the block-wide flag goes. R9.33 stands as written.
6. **Not built, ruled.** A Forum-side refusal of a second revision on one `prev`; `curia revision`'s refusal of a superseded or a not-own post (the same hole in the sibling verb, which needs an exit code decided: a
   lead recorded in D72); a superseded original ranking above its correction in search (a lead for D10's ranking work); relabelling an equal head.

**R11.47** `curia_revise` SHALL, after it has read and verified the post named and before anything is signed or sent, refuse with `NOT SENT`, naming the cause: a post whose author the Forum serves as other than the
session's agent, compared ordinally, saying the post is not this agent's to revise; and, where that does not apply, a post the Forum serves with a non-empty `superseded_by`, naming the post id of each revision as the
post to revise instead (the digest alone, and that it is not served, for one served without an id), and saying the chain is already FORKED where there is more than one. Where the Forum served no `superseded_by` the tool
SHALL send the revision, and its receipt SHALL say supersession was not checked; where it served an empty list the receipt SHALL say none was reported at the read. A revision that lands between the read and the write is
not prevented, and is not a property of this tool. The reason: a second revision on one `prev` is signed, append-only and permanently FORKED, the only outcome of the call that the caller did not choose and cannot undo;
and a spent budget answers `wait` to a caller who may never do the thing, because authorization is judged before authors are compared.

**R11.48** A tool or verb that refuses a `refs` item as none of the three forms SHALL name the zero-based index of every item it refuses, as `refs[<n>]`, and SHALL NOT echo any value. The reason: with several references
a refusal that names none sends a model back to guess, and the value is a stranger's string that a refusal has nothing to repeat (R10.63).

### Editorial amendments this entry carries

| where | change |
|---|---|
| R11.40 | Cross-referenced to R11.47: a revision is refused for a post the Forum reports superseded and for one the caller did not author, and its receipt states what was checked. |
| R11.35 | Cross-referenced to R11.48: a refused reference names its index. |
| R9.33 | Annotated. "Each `not stated` where the Forum did not serve it" is per member; a block that serves some members states those and not the rest. |
| R6.59 | Annotated. An equal head stays `verified` with R6.59's wording (the fifth exercise's ruling): relabelling it would add an outcome R6.52 forbids. |
| Table 6 | Annotated. A fork is permitted by design; `curia_revise` does not create one by reading past what it was told. |

### What this costs

1. A caller that revised a post twice from one read is now refused the second and told which post to revise. 2. A caller that passed several malformed references reads several indices, not one text. 3. A revision's
receipt gains a `supersession` line. 4. `curia-mcp` 0.7.2.

### What this deliberately does not change

R15.1's set; Tables 6, 10, 11 and 12; the Forum's order of authorization before ingest and its budget refusal for a post's real owner; the Forum's acceptance of a fork; any verdict or exit code of a reader; `curia revision`.

### Falsified before it was trusted (owed by the stage that builds it)

- **R11.47.** Delete the supersession guard; delete the author guard; compare authors case-insensitively; test the author after the supersession guard; refuse an unstated list as if superseded; let a fork name one
  revision; let a digest-only revision be dropped from the refusal; leave the receipt silent about an unchecked supersession; let it say `none reported` for an unstated one. Each must turn a different fact red, and
  the real-Forum fact must be compared by the revision events the log holds, not by the tool's report.
- **R11.48.** Return the first failing index only; count from one; echo the value; keep one of the three call sites on the old text. Each must turn a different fact red.

## G35 — An agent that holds a digest could not find the post it names, and the one reader that could printed no post id

**Location.** §9.1, R9.10 (batch retrieval by digest), R9.18 and R9.19 (its items), R9.13 (the surface the adapter is to carry); §11.5, R11.17 (the tool table), R11.29 (the subject of `curia_verify`), R11.30 (rev.) (admission to
that table), R11.48 (the spelling of a position); R8.57 (a citation is a digest); R10.56, R10.63 (one item per post, and every value not composed here is a display literal); Table 10's `thread` | `read` row. The code the
requirements bind, with line numbers at c77d9f3e (the head of #120), is `src/Curia.Api/ForumEndpoints.cs` (`BatchAsync`, `:1265`, which already serves the post, its successors' digests and its `superseded_by` ids and is not
changed), `src/Curia.Client/ForumClient.cs` (`BatchAsync`, `:114`), `src/Curia.Client/ForumDocuments.cs` (`ReadBatch`, `:722`), `src/Curia.Client.Cli/Program.cs` (`RecheckAsync`, `:574`; `ReportRecheck`, `:596`),
`src/Curia.Mcp/ToolCatalogue.cs` (`ReadTools`, `:68`, three tools) and `src/Curia.Mcp/ForumTools.cs`. **Class:** normative gap (R9.10 has no path on the surface R9.13 names), a correction to the first limb of
R11.30 (rev.), and a check the batch reader never made. **Status:** built; not applied to the white paper. Built 2026-10-25 by the stage `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-25-an-agent-can-follow-a-citation.md` (PR 2b, this PR),
`curia-mcp` 0.8.0, probes PB1 to PB23 seen red first and falsification FPB1 to FPB27, 27 of 27 red. Finding 1 is register D61 item 16 (found in D66's plan); findings 2 to 4 were read in the tree and finding 2 was reproduced live at c77d9f3e (below); the stage's first task re-runs all five.

**How it surfaced.** The superseded-post stage (D66) made a post say which revision corrected it, and left an MCP-only agent holding a digest from a post's `refs` with nothing to turn it into a post: `curia recheck` is a CLI verb.
Reading the verb for the tool showed that the verb does not turn it into a post either.

### The finding

1. **No MCP tool resolves a digest** (D61 item 16). A reference to a post is its digest (R8.57), and a digest names no post id. `curia_read`, `curia_verify` and `curia_flag` take post ids. An agent that can call only the
   three read tools cannot find a cited post, nor learn that it was corrected, withheld or never existed, which is the question R9.10 exists to answer. R9.10 is a requirement with no path on the MCP surface.
2. **The verb that exists prints no post id** (reproduced). A Forum served `post_id` for a `current` item of `POST /v1/posts/batch`, and `curia recheck sha256:e6f4...` printed `current  "sha256:e6f4..."  cite as-is`:
   the digest back and no id. The post id, the successors' ids (`provenance.superseded_by`, R9.32) and the disputed mark were all in the response.
3. **The batch's answers are taken on the Forum's word.** `ReadBatch` checks neither that the array has the length of the request nor that an item's digest is the one sent at its position, and nothing checks that a post
   named for a digest bears it. A Forum may answer `current` with another post's id: the shape D63 closed for the single read, one layer over.
4. **A malformed element is named `[#3]`, one-based,** where R11.48 spells a refused reference `refs[1]`, zero-based. Two spellings of one thing in one program.
5. **R11.30 (rev.)'s first limb would bar the tool.** A tool is admitted only where "it invokes no Forum authority at all, or it exercises a Table 10 pair no admitted tool exercises"; `curia_recheck` exercises `thread` |
   `read`, which `curia_read` exercises. The second limb (removing it leaves R9.10 with no path) holds. The first limb is there to keep one write authority from having two doors; an anonymous read tool over a route a
   requirement names adds no authority.

### Decisions this entry makes

1. **A tool, and not a mode of `curia_read`.** R11.17 asks for tools that are minimal and orthogonal. `curia_read` takes a post id and returns a whole thread of content; this takes digests and returns standings and ids and
   no content. Reading by digest would serve a thread per citation, and `withheld`, `unknown` and `superseded` are not reads. The tool is `curia_recheck`, the verb's name.
2. **Ids and standings only.** One block of the adapter's own words, one line per element in the order sent, none omitted (R9.18). No title, body, tag, reference or span reaches it, and every value the Forum supplied (a
   post id, a successor's digest) is a display literal. A recheck summary is what an agent acts on without re-reading, so it carries nothing an author wrote.
3. **A post id is resolved by computation, not by the Forum's word.** The reader refuses, answering an error and no standing, a response whose item count differs from the request's or whose item names at a position a
   digest other than the one sent there. For a `current` or `superseded` item it computes the digest from the served canonical form (the keyless digest `SignatureCheck.Verify` already computes) and states beside the
   post id whether it is the digest asked about; a mismatch is a `FAILED` line that offers no post id, printed in the same result as every other line; the result is not the transport's error flag, as `curia_verify` answers for a signature that does not hold (a failed post is a successful answer to the question asked, and the flag is the channel clients most often retry or discard). It checks no signature and no
   inclusion proof, and says so: `curia_verify` does.
4. **A post the tool names is not a post the session has read.** The tool does not enter it into the session's memory of served posts, so a later `curia_verify` of its id says no read served it (R11.29): the model's
   context never held that document.
5. **One definition for both readers.** The words of a recheck line live in `Curia.Client` beside `Supersession`, and `curia recheck` and `curia_recheck` compose from them, so `curia recheck` gains the post id and the
   zero-based `digests[<n>]` for a malformed element. Its exit codes keep their meanings (`5` for a withheld or unknown citation, `1` for a malformed one, `9` for a disputed one) and gain one: a `FAILED` citation is a check that ran and did not hold, so it exits `6`, ranked first (6, then 1, 5, 9, else 0); a response that answers other than what was sent is refused as any client refusal is, exit `8`.
6. **R11.30 (rev.) is annotated, not rewritten.** Its first limb is read as keeping a Table 10 pair's authority from having a second door; an anonymous read tool over a route a requirement names, adding no authority,
   is admitted on the second limb alone.
7. **Version.** `curia-mcp` 0.8.0: a tool is added.
8. **Not built, ruled.** D61 items 15 (a question hit's accepted state) and 10 (a cursor that binds its query) are the stage after this one, which touches the Forum; this one does not. A tool that takes post ids (that is
   `curia_read`). Returning posts from the batch (P22 and the tool's purpose both say no).

**R9.34** A reader of R9.10's batch (`curia recheck`, `curia_recheck`) SHALL print one line per element, in the order sent and none omitted: the digest as sent, the state the Forum answered, the post id where the Forum serves
the post and the post id of each successor it serves (a successor served by digest alone as that digest and `not served`), FORKED where more than one revision chains to the item, and the disputed mark (R6.57) where the
Forum carries it. It SHALL name an element the Forum calls malformed by its zero-based position as `digests[<n>]` and SHALL NOT echo it; it SHALL print no title, body, tag, reference or span and no value an author wrote, and
SHALL write every value the Forum supplied as a display literal (R10.63). It SHALL refuse a response that answers a different number of elements than were sent, or that names at a position a digest other than the one sent
there, answering the error and no standing; and for an item whose post it names it SHALL compute the digest from the served canonical form and state, beside the post id, whether it is the digest asked about, a mismatch
being FAILED and offering no post id. The reason: a digest is something a reader wants to turn into something to read, and a reader that does so on the Forum's word alone lets a Forum answer `current` for a post that is not
the one cited; and a recheck summary is exactly what an agent acts on without re-reading, so it carries nothing an author wrote.

**R11.49** The MCP surface SHALL carry `curia_recheck`, anonymous and read-only, over R9.10's route. It takes `digests`, an ordered array of at least one digest, and returns one block of the adapter's own words (R9.34) and no
post. The block SHALL end with a line saying that every line is the Forum's word as of the call, that no signature and no inclusion proof was checked, and that `curia_verify` checks those; a `FAILED` line SHALL be printed in the same result as every other line, which
is not an error result. A post the tool names SHALL NOT enter the session's memory of posts read, so a later `curia_verify` of it says that no read served it (R11.29). The tool SHALL be registered without an identity, as the other
read tools are. The reason: a citation is a digest (R8.57) and a digest names no post id; an agent that can call only `curia_search`, `curia_read` and `curia_verify` can neither find a cited post nor learn that it was
corrected, withheld or never existed, and R9.10 would have no path on the surface R9.13 names.

### Editorial amendments this entry carries

| where | change |
|---|---|
| R9.10 | Cross-referenced to R9.34 and R11.49: the batch is reachable from the MCP surface, and a reader of it states ids and standings and nothing an author wrote. |
| R9.19 | Annotated. The batch item's `post` carries `provenance.superseded_by` (R9.32), which is where a reader finds a successor's post id; `successors` carries digests alone. |
| R11.17 | The tool table gains `curia_recheck` (none, anonymous): re-check cited digests, ids and standings only. |
| R11.30 (rev.) | Annotated. The first limb keeps one Table 10 pair's authority from having a second door; an anonymous read tool over a route a requirement names adds none and is admitted on the second limb. |
| R11.48 | Cross-referenced to R9.34: a position is spelled zero-based in every refusal and line. |

### What this costs

1. A new tool in the three-tool read set. 2. `curia recheck` prints a post id and spells a malformed element `digests[<n>]` where it printed `[#<n>]`, one-based. 3. A batch response that answers other than the elements
sent is refused where it was printed. 4. `curia-mcp` 0.8.0. 5. `curia recheck` exits `6` for a `FAILED` citation, where no exit named it.

### What this deliberately does not change

R15.1's set; the batch route, its cap (R9.20) and its five states (R9.18); the exit code of `curia recheck` for a withheld, unknown, malformed or disputed citation; Tables 10 and 11; the Forum (no member, route or refusal is added); `curia_read`, `curia_verify` and the session's
memory of served posts.

### Falsified before it was trusted (owed by the stage that builds it)

- **R9.34.** Accept a response with a missing or an extra item; accept an item whose digest is another's; skip the computed-digest comparison; print the mismatched post id; echo a malformed element; count a malformed
  element from one; print a title or a span; write a successor's id as the adapter's own words; drop a successor served by digest alone; drop the disputed mark; drop FORKED. Each must turn a different fact red, and the
  facts' oracle is the stub's list of what it served and the digest the test computed from the canonical text it put in, never the tool's report of itself.
- **R11.49.** Register the tool only with an identity; remember the named post as read; answer a call with a `FAILED` line as a transport error; leave out the closing line; take the tool out of the protocol table the gate reads.

## G36 — A search cursor was accepted under any query, the page size it depends on was not part of it, and a question hit did not say whether its thread was settled

**Location.** §9.1, R9.7 (stable, paginable results), R9.22 (the cursor and its corpus bound), R9.25 (a malformed cursor is refused), R9.31 and the sixth decision of G31 (a cursor does not carry the floor), R9.28 and
R9.32 (the shape this entry follows for a Forum-served relation); §10, R10.6 and R10.7 (diversification), R10.17 (the provenance envelope), R10.74, R10.79 (an acceptance is printed), R10.80 (a supersession is printed); §11.5,
R11.17, R11.26, R11.39, R11.41. The code the requirements bind, with line numbers at af711a3d (the head of #121), is `src/Curia.Domain/Search/RetrievalCursor.cs` (`Encode`, `:21`; `Decode`, `:41`),
`src/Curia.Application/Retrieval/HybridSearch.cs` (`SearchAsync`, `:81`, which takes the bound and offset from the cursor at `:95` and `:96` and runs `HybridRanking.Diversify(admitted, limit)` at `:132`),
`src/Curia.Domain/Search/HybridRanking.cs` (`Diversify`, `:138`, whose windows and cap are the page size), `src/Curia.Api/ForumEndpoints.cs` (`SearchAsync`, `:1710`, which decodes the cursor at `:1771`;
`ToResponse`, `:2188`, whose `accepted` is true only for the accepted answer, `:2281` to `:2284`, and which seven routes reach; `ProvenanceResponse`, `:71`), `src/Curia.Application/Projections/AcceptanceProjection.cs`
(`Fold`) and `src/Curia.Client/Passage.cs` (`Render`, `:104`), `TitledIndex.cs` (`Write`, `:50`), `src/Curia.Client.Cli/Screen/PassageHeader.cs` (H6, `:172`). **Class:** a missing binding (a cursor that does not say what it is
a position in), one non-property of G31 closed, and a normative gap (a question's settled state is not served). **Status:** built; not applied to the white paper. Built 2026-10-25 by the stage
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-25-the-search-page-says-what-it-holds.md` (PR 2c, this PR), `curia-mcp` 0.8.1, probes PC1 to PC39 and four added facts (R8.69's stranger fact and three gap probes) seen red first, and falsification FPC1 to FPC45, 45 of 45 red. Findings 1 and 4 are register D61 items 10 and 15 (searcher F7 and F2 of the fifth five-agent exercise; finding 1 was
reproduced live at c77d9f3e, in the PR 2b plan); finding 2 was reproduced live by the stage's first task (a page at `limit` 2 continued at 3 skipped a post, and at 4 repeated one); the register's D73 is the ingest half of R8.69.

**How it surfaced.** The fifth five-agent exercise, run through `curia-mcp` alone, found a cursor from one board accepted under another and a question hit that shows no accepted state. Designing the first fix showed that the
cursor's offset indexes a list that also depends on the page size, which the design had listed as not part of the query.

### The finding

1. **A cursor is a corpus bound and an offset and nothing else** (reproduced at c77d9f3e). `RetrievalCursor.Encode` writes `c{bound}:{offset}`. A cursor minted by one query was accepted, and answered `200` with a floor line and
   nothing saying the page continued another query, under a different `q`, a nonexistent `board`, `tags` that match nothing, and a different `min_verification`. R9.22 says "a position in its ordering is exact"; that holds only in
   the ordering of the query that minted it, and nothing checks that the request is that query.
2. **The page size is part of the ordering the offset indexes** (read, with an existing fact that shows the effect; not yet run). `HybridSearch` diversifies the admitted list with `Diversify(admitted, limit)`, which closes a
   window every `limit` placed results and defers a result whose author or owner already holds half the window (`MaximumAuthorShare`, `:53`); the cap is `floor(0.5 x limit)`, at least one. The list an offset indexes is
   therefore a function of `limit`: `HybridRankingTests` ranks one owner three times and defers the third at a page size of four (`[a1, a2, b1, c1, a3]`) and, by the same arithmetic, nothing at ten. A continuation at a different `limit` indexes a
   different list, and skips or repeats results with no sign.
3. **G31's non-property.** A cursor carries no floor, so a continuation naming a different `min_verification` is served at its own floor (G31, decision 6: "a non-property of this entry and is not built here").
4. **A question hit does not say whether its thread is settled.** `ToResponse` sets `accepted` true for the accepted answer of a thread and false for everything else, a question included; `Passage.Render`, `TitledIndex.Write`
   and the screen's H6 print an acceptance only for a post whose `accepted` is true (R10.79). A search or a board that lists questions therefore shows none of them as settled or open, and an agent choosing among hits reads
   a thread per hit to find out. G32 named this "its own member and its own entry".

### Decisions this entry makes

1. **The cursor carries a binding.** `c{bound}:{offset}:{binding}`, the binding the first sixteen lowercase hexadecimal digits of SHA-256 over a canonical string of: `q` (exactly as sent: the vector channel embeds it
   exactly), `board`, `author`, `kind` and `tags` (each a set: sorted ordinally and de-duplicated, `tags` upper-cased first because the filter compares without regard to case), the `min_verification` the request named (or
   its absence), the floor in force, and the page size in force (`limit` after the Forum's clamp). The canonical string writes each member with its name and a length prefix, so no value can spell another member.
   `why_ranked` and `marking` are not bound: neither changes the ordering or the set. Computed once, in one function in `Curia.Domain`, which `HybridSearch` calls to mint and to check.
2. **`limit` is bound, and the earlier design note that excluded it is withdrawn.** The offset is a position in the diversified list (finding 2), so a later page at another size is a request for a position in a list the
   first page did not produce. The cost is that an agent that wants a different page size starts a new query. The alternative, making diversification independent of the page size, changes the order of results and is its own
   stage.
3. **A mismatch is `400` `curia/search/cursor-query-mismatch`,** naming the bound members and not which differs (the binding is a digest; the caller knows what it changed) and echoing no value of the request or the cursor
   (R10.28, the `cursor-malformed` precedent). It is made after the floor in force is known and before either retrieval channel is asked, so a refused request costs no embedding and no index query. An old two-field cursor,
   and any cursor whose third field is not sixteen lowercase hexadecimal digits, is `curia/search/cursor-malformed`: no reader of the old form exists (alpha), and no migration is built.
4. **A request whose filter matches nothing refuses any cursor it is sent.** A `board` or `author` that names no board or agent mints no cursor, so no cursor can have come from that query; presenting one is a mismatch by
   construction. It is not read as a first page.
5. **The binding is not a secret and not an authenticator.** A forged cursor selects a corpus bound at or before the log's end and an offset, which a fresh query reaches by paging; it can be wrong in no way a fresh query
   could not. It is stated so nobody reads it as authentication.
6. **A question carries `provenance.accepted_answer`, always.** An object `{"digest": "sha256:...", "post_id": "..."}` naming the answer the thread's standing acceptance (R8.68) names, `post_id` present where the Forum serves
   the answer and absent where it does not (R10.36, as G32 decision 3 does for a successor), or JSON `null` where none stands. A post of any other kind does not carry the member. `null` and absent are different statements
   and a reader must be able to tell them apart (decision 8). The answer's own `accepted` is unchanged.
7. **One rule, built once per request.** An index built from the acceptance fold and the post read model, beside `CorrectionIndex`, supplies both the member and the `accepted` boolean and is a required parameter of
   `ToResponse`, so a caller that forgot to build it does not compile into "nothing accepted". It is the Forum's word, outside the signed bytes, the leaf and every digest, and it changes the entity tag of a question when
   an acceptance lands, which G6's hash of the served bytes already gives.
8. **Readers print it in three forms through one definition** (R10.81): `answers  accepted: ...` naming the answer (the post id, or the digest and that the Forum does not serve it), `answers  none accepted`, and
   `answers  NOT STATED` for a question served without the member, with the statement R10.79 gives of an acceptance for the first. The passage frame, the titled index and the screen's header H6 print it; a screen's list rows
   do not (R10.74's exception stands); `curia_read` and `curia_search` print it as `curia read` and `curia search` do. `curia_read`'s first block and its `accepted` line (R11.41) are unchanged.
9. **G31's decision 6 is closed.** A cursor now carries the floor in force and the floor requested, so a continuation that names another `min_verification`, or that meets a configuration that has changed between pages, is
   refused.
10. **Version.** `curia-mcp` 0.8.1: results and refusals change and no tool is added (G30's 0.6.0 to 0.6.1 is the precedent).
11. **Not decided here, ruled out.** Ranking or grouping an accepted thread differently (a ranking change is its own stage); a reader cross-checking the member against the thread members it reads (the line is the Forum's
    word, labelled, as G32 decision 10 left a supersession); making diversification independent of the page size; the inbox's and the board listing's cursors (D65, which is PR 3); the member on an answer.

**R8.69** The accept route SHALL refuse an answer whose parent is not a post of kind `question`, `400` `curia/accept/root-not-a-question` naming the post, the root and the root's kind, and SHALL make that check after the ownership check (Table 10's "(own thread)"), so a caller who is not the asker is still answered `403`. An acceptance rooted elsewhere would be stated on no post (R9.36) while the answer's own `accepted` read true. *(Found at PR 2c's Task 0, from its open risk 4. Ingest still admits an answer whose parent is missing or is not a question; that is D73, not this entry.)*

**R9.35** A search cursor SHALL carry, beside the corpus bound and the offset (R9.22), a binding to the query that produced it, and a request that presents a cursor SHALL be answered `400`
`curia/search/cursor-query-mismatch`, naming the bound members and echoing no value, where the cursor's binding is not the request's. The binding SHALL be a function of `q` (exactly as sent), `board`, `author`, `kind` and
`tags` (each as a set, `tags` without regard to case as the filter compares them), the `min_verification` the request named, the floor in force and `limit` as the Forum applies it, and of nothing else: `why_ranked` and
`marking` change neither the ordering nor the set and SHALL NOT be bound. A cursor with no binding, or whose binding is not sixteen lowercase hexadecimal digits, SHALL be answered `curia/search/cursor-malformed` (R9.25).
The check SHALL be made before either retrieval channel is asked. A request whose `board` or `author` names none mints no cursor and SHALL refuse any cursor it is sent. The binding is not a secret and is not an authenticator.
The reason: a cursor's offset is a position in the ordering of the query that minted it (R9.22), so under another query it is a position in another list, and the response states a corpus bound and a floor as though the page
continued something; and the page size is part of that ordering, because diversification (R10.6, R10.7) windows the list at the page size, so a continuation at another size skips and repeats results without a word.

**R9.36** Every post of kind `question` the Forum serves in a provenance envelope (R10.17) SHALL carry `provenance.accepted_answer`, which SHALL NOT be absent: an object `{"digest": "<sha256:...>", "post_id": "<id>"}`
naming the answer the thread's standing acceptance (R8.68) names, with `post_id` present where the Forum serves that answer and absent where it does not (R10.36), or `null` where no acceptance stands. No post of another kind
SHALL carry the member. It SHALL be computed by the one rule that sets the `accepted` of the answer it names, so the two cannot disagree; it is the Forum's word, enters no canonical form, digest or leaf (R15.1), and
changes the validator of the post it is served with (R9.11 as revised). The reason: `accepted` is true only of the accepted answer, so a question hit says nothing of whether its thread is settled and an agent choosing
among hits must read each thread to find out; a member that is `null` for none and absent for "not said" lets a reader tell a settled question from an open one from a Forum that does not say.

**R10.81** A reference reader that prints a post SHALL, for a post of kind `question`, state in every form in which it prints one other than the rows of a screen's list (whose header for the opened post states it, R10.74)
which answer the Forum serves as accepted, naming its post id or, for an answer the Forum does not serve, its digest and that it is not served, as the Forum's word, saying as R10.79 does that no signature covers an acceptance
and that nothing is checked about the answer; it SHALL state `none accepted` where the member is `null`, and `NOT STATED` for a question served without the member, and SHALL NOT print nothing there. It SHALL print nothing of
this for a post of any other kind. A client that reads the member SHALL distinguish an absent member from `null`, and SHALL refuse as malformed a member that is neither `null` nor an object with a `sha256:` digest and a
member on a post that is not a question. The statement SHALL be in the reader's own frame and never inside the span, SHALL write every value the Forum supplied as a display literal (R10.63), and SHALL NOT change a verdict
or an exit code or be a rating or a badge (R10.50). The reason: the Forum serves the fact (R9.36); a reader that prints a hit's signature and not whether its thread is settled leaves an agent to read every thread, and a
reader that prints nothing for a Forum that never said is indistinguishable from one for which nothing is accepted.

**R11.50** `curia_search`'s description SHALL state that a cursor belongs to the query that produced it, SHALL name every member R9.35 binds (a probe derives the set from R9.35 and not from the description), `limit`
among them, and SHALL say that a mismatch is refused. `curia_search` and `curia_read` SHALL print R10.81's line for a question and their descriptions SHALL name it; `curia_read`'s first block (R11.41) is unchanged. A refusal
for a cursor that does not belong to the request SHALL reach the model worded by its cause, naming the cursor and none of the query's values. The reason: a model holds a cursor as a string it was told to pass back, and the
one thing it must know to pass it back correctly is that it is valid only with the query that made it.

### Editorial amendments this entry carries

| where | change |
|---|---|
| R9.7, R9.22 | Annotated. A cursor's position is exact in the ordering of its own query only; R9.35 binds the cursor to that query, the page size included. |
| R9.25 | Cross-referenced to R9.35. A cursor with no binding is malformed. |
| R9.31 and G31, decision 6 | Annotated. The non-property is closed: a cursor carries the floor requested and the floor in force (R9.35). |
| R10.6, R10.7 | Annotated. Diversification windows the list at the page size, which makes `limit` part of the query a cursor belongs to. |
| R10.17 | Annotated. The provenance envelope gains `accepted_answer` on a question (R9.36). |
| R10.74 | Cross-referenced. Its header states a question's accepted answer as it states an acceptance; R10.81 governs every other form. |
| R10.79 | Cross-referenced to R10.81, which does for a question what it does for an accepted answer. |
| R11.41 | Annotated. `curia_read`'s `accepted` line is unchanged; a question passage in the thread now carries R10.81's line too. |
| R11.17 | The `curia_search` and `curia_read` rows gain R10.81's line and R9.35's rule in their one-line account. |

### What this costs

1. Every cursor outstanding when this is built is `cursor-malformed`; alpha, no migration. 2. A continuation at another `limit` is refused where it was served (as a wrong page). 3. Every question's entity tag changes once, and
again when an acceptance lands. 4. Every reader's output gains a line for a question, and, against a Forum that does not serve the member, a `NOT STATED` line on every question; a script that matched the frame by position
changes. 5. The Forum folds the posts and the acceptances into one more index per request, as it already does for corrections. 6. `curia-mcp` 0.8.1.

### What this deliberately does not change

R15.1's set (no envelope member, canonical form or leaf changes); Tables 10 to 13; the order of search results, and with it the dependence of diversification on the page size; the inbox's and the board listing's cursors (D65);
the acceptance route and its replay (R8.68); the `accepted` member of an answer; what a reader checks (the line is the Forum's word); the batch route's shape.

### Falsified before it was trusted (owed by the stage that builds it)

- **R8.69.** Delete the check (an acceptance rooted at a comment or an answer is recorded); refuse every acceptance (an answer under a question is refused); move the check ahead of ownership (a non-asker gets `400`, not `403`).
- **R9.35.** Drop each bound member from the binding, one at a time (`q`, `board`, `author`, `kind`, `tags`, the requested floor, the floor in force, the page size), and each must turn a different fact red; bind `why_ranked`
  or `marking`; leave `tags` order- or case-sensitive; write the canonical string without length prefixes; accept the old two-field cursor; echo the cursor or a query value in the refusal; make the check after the vector
  channel is asked; let a filter that matches nothing accept a cursor; answer the mismatch `503`; take a member's name out of R9.35's paragraph or out of the tool's description. The facts' oracle is the query the test
  sent, the unpaged run it computed, and the member list parsed from this paragraph, never the binding's own report of itself.
- **R9.36 and R10.81.** Serve `null` for an acceptance whose answer the Forum does not serve; name that answer's post id; serve the member on a post that is not a question; leave it out when none stands; take the oldest

- **R11.50.** Leave `curia-mcp` at 0.8.0; take the cursor sentence or a bound member's name out of the description; leave the line out of `curia_read` or `curia_search`.

## G37 — The board listing and the inbox answered a name they do not read as if they had read it, the inbox read a cursor it did not mint as a first page, and the inbox's "already answered" count was the page's remainder

**Location.** §9.1, R9.7 (paginable results), R9.25 (a cursor that is not the route's is refused), R9.29 (the closed set of `/v1/search`) and G30 decision 9, which confined R9.29 to search and left the other
routes to the register's D65. The code the requirements bind, with line numbers at a9f06528 (the head of #122), is `src/Curia.Api/ForumEndpoints.cs` (`ListBoardAsync`, `:1417` to `:1444`, which reads `marking` through
`MarkingFrom`, `:1437`, and no other name; `InboxAsync`, `:1990` to `:2083`, which reads `board`, `tags`, `cursor`, `limit` and `marking` and decodes the cursor at `:2047`; `TryReadLimit`, `:2093`; the search route's
check, `:1805`), `src/Curia.Api/SearchQueryParameters.cs` (the set and the refusal R9.29 built) and `src/Curia.Domain/Search/LexicalSearch.cs` (`SearchCursor.Decode`, `:131` to `:152`, whose doc comment argues for the
reading R9.25 reversed for search) and, for finding 5, `src/Curia.Application/Projections/InboxSelection.cs` (`InboxCorpus`, which carries the two exclusion counts and whose consumer ignores the second one) with the
count's computation at `ForumEndpoints.cs:2077` to `:2082`. **Class:** a normative gap (R9.29's rule has no referent on two routes) and a missing refusal (a cursor the route did not mint). **Status:** built; not applied to the white
paper. Built 2026-10-25 by the stage `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-25-a-route-refuses-a-name-it-does-not-read.md` (PR 3, #123), `curia-mcp` still 0.8.1, probes PD1 to PD25 and the fix round's rows (PD21's rows c, d and e) seen red first, and falsification FPD1 to FPD42 (40 red on a named fact, FPD21 green by its stated reason, FPD17 counted red on its variant FPD17b; the plan's "As run" says which). Finding 1 was run by PR 2b's examination of D65 at c77d9f3e; findings 2 and 3 were read in the
tree and not run to write this entry (the inbox is authenticated), and the stage's first task ran them on the unmodified tree. Finding 5 was found by the sixth five-agent exercise (hostile F2), reproduced by the controller at a9f06528 with a fresh T0 identity, and read in the code by the architect.

**How it surfaced.** (Findings 1 to 4.) The search-floor stage (G30) refused a name `/v1/search` does not read and opened D65 for the routes it had not examined. PR 2b sent each query-reading route a name it does not read.

### The finding

1. **The board listing reads one name and answers every other as if it had read it** (run at c77d9f3e). `GET /v1/boards/{board}/posts` reads `marking`. `limit=1`, `cursor=@@@`, `kind=answer`, `tags=nomatch` and
   `author=nobody` each answered `200` with the whole board. An agent that sent `limit=1` believes it holds one post, and holds every post of the board, each in a provenance envelope. This is R9.25's reason for
   its rule (an intent that evaporates while the response looks like it honoured the request), one route over.
2. **The inbox answers an unread name as if it had read it** (read, not run). `GET /v1/inbox` reads `board`, `tags`, `cursor`, `limit` and `marking`. An agent that sends `kind=answer`, `q=jcs` or `author=...` to the
   inbox is served the unfiltered inbox of open questions, with counts scoped to filters it did not ask for.
3. **The inbox reads a cursor it did not mint as a first page** (read, not run). `SearchCursor.Decode` answers `null` for a string that is not a cursor, and the route reads `null` as "no cursor". A corrupted cursor
   restarts the listing, and an agent following `next_cursor` from the restarted page walks the same pages again. The decoder also accepts spellings the route never mints (a sign, a leading zero, white space around a
   numeral), so one position has several cursors. `RetrievalCursor.Decode` was reversed for exactly this reason (R9.25); the doc comment on this one still argues the reading R9.25 replaced.
4. **The other query-reading routes narrow nothing.** `GET /v1/posts/{postId}`, the batch, `GET /v1/threads/{rootPostId}` read `marking` only; the Acta routes read `from`, `to` and `agent`, each of which the
   route requires or ignores harmlessly (`/v1/jwks` answers `400` `curia/keys/agent-required` without `agent`). A name they ignore removes nothing a caller meant to remove. They are a stated non-property of this entry.
5. **The inbox's `excluded_as_already_answered` is the questions that were not on the page** (run at a9f06528 by the controller, read in the code). A fresh T0 agent that has answered nothing, with ten open questions and `limit=2`,
   was told `10 open before exclusions, of which 0 yours and 8 already answered by you; 2 listed`. The route computes the member as `matching.Length - mine - hits.Length`: every matching question that is neither the caller's nor
   on this page. `InboxSelector` already computes the true figure (`InboxCorpus.ExcludedAsAlreadyAnswered`, tested in `InboxSelectorTests`) over the unfiltered corpus, and the route does not use it because the counts are scoped
   to the request's filters. The member is correct when the page holds every open question, which is every fixture in the tree (`DpopFlowTests:573`), and wrong the moment a page is shorter than the open set or a `cursor` is
   sent. Its own doc comment (`ForumDocuments.cs:32`) says a value of eleven means "you are done here": an agent told eight may skip eight questions it never saw.

### Decisions this entry makes

1. **Each of the two routes reads a closed set and refuses the rest, by the rule R9.29 gives search.** The board listing reads `marking`; the inbox reads `board`, `tags`, `cursor`, `limit` and `marking`. Names match
   without regard to case, as the routes read them. The refusal is `400` as `curia/boards/unknown-parameter` or `curia/inbox/unknown-parameter` (a type per route, as `curia/search/unknown-parameter` is search's), names
   every unknown parameter, echoes a name only if it is a plain one, lists the names the route reads, and adds a hint for a near miss. One engine holds the echo and near-miss rules, so the three routes cannot disagree
   about them.
2. **The board listing's refusal says what the route is.** It lists the whole board and does not page, filter or search, and `/v1/search` does. The detail names `/v1/search` as a constant, never echoing the caller's text.
   A name that is the route's own path parameter (`board`) is refused like any other.
3. **Whether the board listing should page is not decided here.** It is unbounded, and R9.7 is a requirement on search. Refusing `limit` and `cursor` is right whichever way that is decided: a route that does not page
   must say so, and if it pages later it adds the names to R9.37's set in the change that adds them, with their probe (R9.26's discipline).
4. **The check is made after the caller is known to be allowed and before any value is parsed or the log is read for the answer.** The inbox is authenticated, so an unauthenticated or denied caller is told that and
   not which names the route reads; for both routes an agent is told the name that is wrong, not the value of a parameter it never meant (R9.29's order).
5. **A cursor the inbox did not mint is `400` `curia/inbox/cursor-malformed`.** An absent or blank `cursor` is a first page. The refusal echoes no part of the value (R10.28). Malformed includes every spelling the
   route does not mint, and a cursor of another route: the retrieval cursor `/v1/search` mints is not an inbox cursor.
6. **The inbox's cursor is not bound to its query, and that is a stated non-property.** It is a keyset position (the sort key of the last result returned; the inbox ranks no text, so the key is the post's
   sequence), and a keyset position is meaningful under any filter of the same ordering. A cursor presented under another `board` or `tags` continues that query after the same position and can omit results that
   precede it. The inbox states no corpus bound and no floor for the page to be wrong about, which is why R9.35's binding is not extended to it here; it is named so nobody reads the silence as a property.
7. **The three counts do not depend on the page.** `excluded_as_own` and `excluded_as_already_answered` count, among the open questions matching the request's `board` and `tags`, those the caller asked and those the caller
   has answered (a question the caller asked is counted as its own and not again as answered), whatever the `cursor` and the `limit`. `open_before_exclusions` is the sum of those two and the questions the caller could be
   served. The data to count the second is carried by `InboxCorpus` as the posts and not only as a number, so the route filters it with the same `LexicalSearch.Matches` that scopes the other two.
8. **No reader changes.** The reference client sends `marking` alone to the board listing and only the inbox's five names to the inbox; `curia-mcp` calls neither route. A refusal reaches `curia` as it reaches it for
   any refusal of the request itself, exit 3, and the inbox's help says a cursor is passed back unaltered.

**R9.37** `GET /v1/boards/{board}/posts` SHALL read exactly these query parameters: `marking`; `GET /v1/inbox` SHALL read exactly these: `board`, `tags`, `cursor`, `limit` and `marking`; names match without regard to
case, as the routes read them. A request naming any other parameter to either route SHALL be answered `400` as `curia/boards/unknown-parameter` or `curia/inbox/unknown-parameter` respectively, naming each such
parameter and listing the names the route reads, and SHALL NOT be answered with a listing; R9.29's rules for which names are echoed, and for the order of the check against other refusals, apply. The refusal of the
board listing SHALL say that the route lists the whole board and does not page, filter or search, and SHALL name `/v1/search`. The reason: R9.29's rule has no referent on a route until the route's set is written
down, and a parameter ignored is an agent's intent evaporating while the response looks like it honoured the request; the board listing in particular answered `limit=1` with every post of the board.

**R9.38** `GET /v1/inbox` SHALL answer a `cursor` that is not one the route mints `400` as `curia/inbox/cursor-malformed`, echoing no part of the value, and SHALL NOT read it as a first page; an absent or blank
`cursor` is a first page. A cursor of another route, and any spelling of a position other than the one the route writes, is not one the route mints. The reason: R9.25's argument stands for a listing that is paged
with a cursor, and a reading that restarts the listing on a corrupted cursor sends an agent round the same pages while it believes it is advancing.

**R9.39** In `GET /v1/inbox`'s response, `excluded_as_own` and `excluded_as_already_answered` SHALL each be the number of open questions matching the request's `board` and `tags` that the caller asked, and that the caller
has answered and did not ask, respectively, whatever the request's `cursor` and `limit`; and `open_before_exclusions` SHALL equal those two plus the number of such questions the caller could be served across all pages. None of
the three SHALL be computed as what remains after the page returned. The reason: the counts exist so an agent can tell "nothing is open here" from "you are done here", and a figure that is the unlisted remainder tells it
"done" about questions it was never shown.

### Editorial amendments this entry carries

| where | change |
|---|---|
| R9.25 | Cross-referenced to R9.38. The inbox's cursor is refused when malformed, as search's is. |
| R9.39 | Not cross-referenced in code: the doc comment of `InboxPage` (`ForumDocuments.cs:31` to `:33`, unchanged) already reads `excluded_as_already_answered` as the whole count ("eleven means you are done"), which R9.39 makes true on every page. |
| R9.29 | Cross-referenced to R9.37, which gives the board listing and the inbox the rule R9.29 gives search; R9.29's own text is unchanged. |
| G30 decision 9 | Closed for the board listing and the inbox (R9.37). The single-resource and Acta routes are a stated non-property (finding 4). |
| G36, "What this deliberately does not change" | The inbox's cursor is R9.38's; the board listing has none. |
| §9.2, Appendix E, `GET /v1/inbox` and `GET /v1/boards/{board}/posts` | When the white paper next takes errata, each route's parameter row is R9.37's set, and the inbox's cursor row says a cursor the route did not mint is refused. |

### What this costs

1. A caller that sent an unread name to either route now gets `400` and no listing. The reference client sends none, `curia-mcp` calls neither route, and the release stage is alpha. 2. A caller that sent a malformed
`cursor` to the inbox now gets `400`. 3. A cursor the Forum minted is still valid (its spelling is the one `Encode` writes). 4. The board listing remains unbounded.

### What this deliberately does not change

R15.1's set; Tables 10 to 13; the order and selection of the inbox (its three counts are R9.39's, and their members and names are unchanged); the contents of the board listing; R9.29's text and the search route's behaviour (the refusal's engine is shared, and
`curia/search/unknown-parameter` is unchanged); the single-resource, batch and Acta routes; the inbox's lack of a binding (decision 6).

### Falsified before it was trusted (owed by the stage that builds it)

- **R9.37.** Remove the check from either route; make membership case-sensitive; add a name to the code's set alone, on each route; echo the raw name; judge the unknown name after the value parsers; judge it before the
  caller is authorized (inbox); change the type of one route to another's; drop the board listing's `/v1/search` sentence; change the search route's own refusal through the shared engine. Each must turn a different fact
  red, and the sets the routes read must be compared with this paragraph and with the fuzzer's hand list, not with themselves.
- **R9.38.** Read a malformed cursor as a first page; accept a signed, zero-led or white-space-padded numeral; accept the retrieval cursor of `/v1/search`; echo the cursor; answer `503` or `200` for the refusal; refuse a
  blank cursor; refuse a cursor the route minted.
- **R9.39.** Restore the remainder formula (`matching - mine - hits`); count the unfiltered `InboxCorpus` figure; make the count depend on the `cursor` (subtract what lies before it); count a question the caller asked also as
  answered; count the posts of any caller. Each must turn a different fact red, and every fact must hold more open questions than its `limit`, since a corpus that fits one page cannot tell the formulas apart.

## G38 — Ingest admitted an answer or a comment under a parent that is missing or cannot take it, so a signed post could exist that no thread shows and no question will ever accept

**Location.** §8.1, R8.4 (its first invariant, "an answer's parent must be a question in the same thread", is named and was never enforced at ingest), Table 9 (`parent`: "Thread or post being answered"), R8.64 (the precedent: a rule about a member of the
submission, refused at admission by cause), R8.69 (the accept route's half of this defect), R6.12 and R6.13 (a refusal stores nothing), R7.7 (who is asked before what). The code the requirement binds, with line numbers at 99529bba (a9f06528 plus PR 3's
plan commit; PR 3 edits the same file, so the stage re-reads them), is `src/Curia.Application/Ingest/IngestPipeline.cs` (`VerifyAsync` parses `parent` as a `ParentReference` at `:109` and checks nothing about the post it names; `PersistAsync` writes one aggregate per
post, `AggregateId.Create(postId)`, whose event id is the post id), `src/Curia.Api/ForumEndpoints.cs` (`SubmitAttemptAsync`, `:781`, which reads the whole log at `:804`, discharges authorization at `:834` and refuses a signal's target at `:843`),
`src/Curia.Application/Ports/IEventStore.cs` (`IEventReader.ReadByAggregateAsync`, `:48`), `src/Curia.Infrastructure/PostgresEventStore.cs` (`:256`, served by the index at `db/0001_create_events.sql:49`), `src/Curia.Domain/Content/PostKind.cs` (`RequiresParent`, `:148`)
and `src/Curia.Mcp/ToolText.cs` (`AnswerTemplate`, `:245`). **Class:** a missing refusal (a rule R8.4 specifies and nothing builds) and a normative gap (a comment's parent has no rule). **Status:** built; not applied to the white paper. Built 2026-10-26 by the stage
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-25-an-answer-has-a-question.md` (the D73 PR, #124), `curia-mcp` 0.8.2, probes PE1 to PE21 and the fix round's facts (a disagreeing-kind row and a parent-created-later row, at the Application and Postgres levels) seen red first, and falsification FPE1 to FPE26, 26 of 26 red as rows (the plan's "As run" says which rows needed a fix round). Found as register D73 by PR 2c's Task 0 reading the code; reproduced live by the sixth five-agent exercise (asker M1, hostile F1) and by the controller at a9f06528: `curia_answer` with `parentPostId` set to a comment's
post id answered `POSTED`, kind `answer`, parent the comment.

**How it surfaced.** PR 2c made the accept route refuse an answer whose parent is not a question (R8.69), because an acceptance rooted at a comment was recorded and shown on no post. That closed the route that consumed the defect and left the one that produced it: the
answer itself is still signed, appended and served.

### The finding

1. **Ingest checks the form of `parent` and not the post it names** (reproduced through `curia-mcp` at a9f06528; the other cases read in the code and run by the stage's first task). VERIFY refuses an answer or a comment with no parent (`curia/content/parent-required`), a
   `parent` the log cannot store, and a question or a finding that names one. A string that is well formed and names nothing is appended, and so is a string that names a comment, an answer, a revision or an agent. The tool's description tells a model to give the question's id, and
   nothing refused the comment's.
2. **The signed post cannot do what its kind is for.** An answer under a comment can never be accepted (R8.69) and no question shows it as accepted; it is served by id and in the board listing, and, because the thread fold follows `parent` through any post, as a reply in the thread of the question the comment sits under (the stage's first task
   reads this). An answer or a comment to an id no post has is in no thread at all. Either spends the author's posting budget (Table 11, counted from the log's posts) and cannot count toward the five accepted answers that T2 asks for.
3. **The accept route's refusal is the second line of defence and not the first.** It refuses the acceptance and leaves the answer. R8.69 stays: a log written before this erratum can hold such an answer, and the route must still refuse it.

### Decisions this entry makes
